sentences.zh: 呂大器

translations.literal: Lu Daqi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Daqi

sentences.zh: 呂大器，字儼若，遂寧人。

translations.literal: Lu Daqi, styled Yanruo, was a native of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Daqi, whose style name was Yanruo, came from Suining.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of the Chongzhen reign.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the first year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 援行人，擢吏部稽勛主事，更歷四司，乞假歸。

translations.literal: Through the yuanyi process he was appointed bearer of decrees, then promoted to director of the Merit Records Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel, served in four departments in turn, and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After entering service through the yuanyi channel, he rose to director of the Merit Records Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel, passed through four bureaus in succession, and asked for leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 以邑城庳惡，倡議修築。

translations.literal: Because the county seat walls were low and in poor condition, he proposed rebuilding them.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the county walls low and unsound, he took the lead in proposing their reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 工甫竣，賊至，佐有司拒守，城獲全。

translations.literal: When the work had just been completed, bandits arrived; he assisted the local officials in holding the defense, and the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: The project had barely been finished when bandits came; he helped the local authorities hold the defense, and the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 詔增秩一等。

translations.literal: An edict increased his rank by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: An edict raised his rank by one grade.

sentences.zh: 出為關南道參議，遷固原副使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as assistant commissioner of the Guannan circuit and transferred to vice commissioner of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as assistant commissioner of the Guannan circuit and was transferred to vice commissioner of Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 巡撫丁啟睿檄大器討長武賊，用穴地火攻法滅之。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Ding Qirui ordered Daqi to suppress the Changwu bandits, and he destroyed them using tunneling and fire-attack methods.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ding Qirui ordered Daqi to campaign against the Changwu bandits, and he wiped them out with tunneling and fire attack.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to right censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 劾總兵官柴時華不法，解其職，立遣副將王世寵代之。

translations.literal: He memorialized the general Chai Shihua for illegal conduct, relieved him of his post, and immediately sent the deputy Wang Shichong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the regional commander Chai Shihua for misconduct, removed him from office, and at once sent the deputy Wang Shichong to replace him.

sentences.zh: 時華乞兵西部及土魯番為變，大器令世寵討敗時華及西部，時華自焚死。

translations.literal: Shihua solicited troops from the western tribes and Turfan to revolt; Daqi ordered Shichong to attack and defeat Shihua and the western forces, and Shihua burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shihua begged troops from the western tribes and Turfan to rise in revolt; Daqi ordered Shichong to attack and defeat Shihua and the western forces, and Shihua burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 塞外爾叠尼、黃臺吉等擁眾乞賞，謀犯肅州，守臣拒走之。

translations.literal: Erdieni, Huang Taiji, and others beyond the frontier gathered their followers to beg rewards and plotted to attack Suzhou; the defending officials repulsed and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the frontier Erdieni, Huang Taiji, and others massed their followers to demand rewards and plotted to strike Suzhou; the defenders drove them back.

sentences.zh: 大器假賞犒名，毒飲馬泉，殺其眾無算。

translations.literal: Daqi, under the pretense of reward and consolation, poisoned the Horse-Drinking Spring and killed their followers without number.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi, under the guise of bestowing rewards, poisoned the Horse-Drinking Spring and slaughtered their followers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 又遣總兵官馬爌督副將世寵等討群番為亂者，斬首七百餘級，撫三十八族而還。

translations.literal: He also sent the general Ma Guan to supervise Deputy General Shichong and others in suppressing the Qiang tribes in revolt; more than seven hundred heads were taken, thirty-eight clans were pacified, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the regional commander Ma Guan to supervise Deputy General Shichong and others in putting down the rebellious Qiang tribes; more than seven hundred heads were taken, thirty-eight clans were pacified, and they returned.

sentences.zh: 又擊敗其餘黨。

translations.literal: He again defeated their remaining partisans.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated their remaining bands as well.

sentences.zh: 西陲略定。

translations.literal: The western frontier was roughly settled.
translations.idiomatic: The western marches were largely pacified.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，擢兵部添註右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year he was promoted to acting right vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year he was promoted to acting right vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 大器負才，性剛躁，善避事。

translations.literal: Daqi was talented but proud, impatient by nature, and skilled at evading responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi was gifted but arrogant, quick-tempered by nature, and adept at shirking duty.

sentences.zh: 見天下多故，懼當軍旅任，力辭，且投揭吏科，言已好酒色財，必不可用。

translations.literal: Seeing that the realm was beset by troubles on every side, he feared being assigned military duties, strove to decline, and even submitted a memorial to the Office of Personnel in the censorate saying he was addicted to wine, women, and wealth and could certainly not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing trouble everywhere in the empire, he dreaded military appointment, pressed hard to decline, and even lodged a memorial with the personnel section of the censorate declaring himself addicted to wine, women, and wealth and utterly unfit for service.

sentences.zh: 帝趣令入京，詭稱疾不至。

translations.literal: The emperor urgently ordered him to enter the capital, but he falsely claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urgently ordered him to the capital, but he feigned illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨切責，亦不至，命所司察奏。

translations.literal: Severe edicts rebuked him sharply, yet still he did not arrive; the throne ordered the relevant offices to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh edicts rebuked him, yet still he did not come; the throne ordered the responsible offices to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 明年三月始至，命以本官兼右僉都御史，總督保定、山東、河北軍務。

translations.literal: Only in the third month of the following year did he arrive; he was ordered to serve in his existing post concurrently as right censor-in-chief with overall command of military affairs in Baoding, Shandong, and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the third month of the following year did he arrive; he was ordered to retain his present office while also serving as right censor-in-chief with overall command of military affairs in Baoding, Shandong, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時畿輔未解嚴，大器及諸將和應薦、張汝行馳扼順義牛欄山。

translations.literal: At the time the capital district had not yet been placed at ease, and Daqi together with the generals He Yingjian and Zhang Ruxing rushed to hold the Niulan Pass area in Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region was still under alert, and Daqi with the generals He Yingjian and Zhang Ruxing hurried to block the Niulan Pass route in Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 總督趙光抃集諸鎮師大戰螺山，應薦陣亡，他將亦多敗。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Zhao Guangbian assembled the troops of the various garrisons for a great battle at Luoshan; Yingjian died in battle and the other generals also suffered many defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhao Guangbian gathered the armies of the garrisons for a great battle at Luoshan; Yingjian fell in battle and the other commanders suffered heavy defeats as well.

sentences.zh: 大器所部無失事，增俸一等。

translations.literal: Daqi's own command suffered no mishap, and his salary was increased by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi's own command met with no mishap, and his salary was raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 五月，以保定息警，罷總督官，特設江西、湖廣、應天、安慶總督，駐九江，大器任之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, because Baoding was quiet, the grand coordinator's post was abolished; a special grand coordinator for Jiangxi, Huguang, Yingtian, and Anqing was established at Jiujiang, and Daqi was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, as Baoding was calm, the grand coordinator was abolished and a special grand coordinator for Jiangxi, Huguang, Yingtian, and Anqing was set up at Jiujiang, with Daqi in the post.

sentences.zh: 湖北地已失，武昌亦陷，左良玉駐九江，稱疾不進。

translations.literal: Most of Hubei had already been lost and Wuchang too had fallen; Zuo Liangyu camped at Jiujiang and claimed illness, refusing to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei was largely lost and Wuchang had fallen; Zuo Liangyu lay at Jiujiang, pleading illness and refusing to advance.

sentences.zh: 以侯恂故疑大器圖己，語具良玉傳中。

translations.literal: Because of Hou Xun he suspected Daqi of plotting against him—the full account is given in Liangyu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Hou Xun he suspected Daqi of scheming against him; the full story is told in Liangyu's biography.

sentences.zh: 大器詣榻前與慰勞，疑稍釋。

translations.literal: Daqi went to his bedside to offer consolation, and the suspicion was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi went to his bedside to console him, and the suspicion eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 而張獻忠大躪湖南，分兵陷袁州、吉安。

translations.literal: But Zhang Xianzhong rampaged through Hunan and sent detachments to seize Yuanzhou and Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhang Xianzhong swept through Hunan and sent columns to take Yuanzhou and Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 大器急遣部將及良玉軍連破之樟樹鎮，峽江、永新二郡皆復。

translations.literal: Daqi urgently dispatched his subordinates together with Liangyu's army to defeat them successively at Zhangshu Town, and both Xiajiang and Yongxin prefectures were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi urgently sent his subordinates with Liangyu's army to defeat them in succession at Zhangshu Town, and both Xiajiang and Yongxin were recovered.

sentences.zh: 已而建昌、撫州陷，良玉、大器不和，兵私鬥，焚南昌關廂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jianchang and Fuzhou fell; Liangyu and Daqi were at odds, the troops fought among themselves in private, and the customs offices of Nanchang were burned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jianchang and Fuzhou fell; Liangyu and Daqi were estranged, the soldiers fought in private, and the customs sheds at Nanchang were burned.

sentences.zh: 廷議因改大器南京兵部右侍郎，以袁繼鹹代。

translations.literal: The court accordingly changed Daqi to right vice minister of War at Nanjing, with Yuan Jixian replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon moved Daqi to right vice minister of War at Nanjing and replaced him with Yuan Jixian.

sentences.zh: 十七年四月，京師報陷，南京大臣議立君。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year, word came that the capital had fallen; the great ministers at Nanjing deliberated on enthroning a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year news came that the capital had fallen; the great ministers at Nanjing debated whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 大器主錢謙益、雷縯祚言，立潞王。

translations.literal: Daqi upheld the views of Qian Qianyi and Lei Zuo and urged enthroning the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi sided with Qian Qianyi and Lei Zuo and argued for enthroning the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 議未定而馬士英及劉澤清諸將擁福王至。

translations.literal: Before the deliberation was settled, Ma Shiying together with Liu Zeqing and other generals brought the Prince of Fu forward.
translations.idiomatic: Before the debate was settled, Ma Shiying with Liu Zeqing and other generals brought forward the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 福王立，遷大器吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Daqi was transferred to left vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu took the throne, Daqi was made left vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大器以異議絀，自危，乃上疏劾士英。

translations.literal: Daqi had been marginalized for dissenting, felt himself endangered, and therefore memorialized impeaching Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: Marginalized for his dissent, Daqi felt himself in peril and memorialized to impeach Shiying.

sentences.zh: 言其擁兵入朝，留政地，翻先皇手定逆案，欲躋阮大鋮中樞。

translations.literal: He said that Shiying had marched troops into court, remained in power, reversed the late emperor's hand-fixed list of traitors, and sought to raise Ruan Dacheng to the center of government.
translations.idiomatic: He charged that Shiying had marched troops into the capital, clung to power, overturned the late emperor's personally fixed list of traitors, and meant to place Ruan Dacheng at the heart of government.

sentences.zh: 其子以銅臭為都督，女弟夫未履行陣，授總戎，姻婭越其傑、田仰、楊文驄先朝罪人，盡登膴仕，亂名器。

translations.literal: His son had been made a regional commander for reeking of money, his sister's husband had been given supreme command though he had not trod a battlefield, and relatives and clients—Yue Qijie, Tian Yang, Yang Wenbi—men condemned in the previous reign, had all been lavished with fat offices, throwing ranks and appointments into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: His son had been made a regional commander for the stink of money, his brother-in-law given supreme command without ever taking the field, and clients such as Yue Qijie, Tian Yang, and Yang Wenbi—condemned men from the previous reign—had all been heaped with lucrative posts, corrupting the order of rank.

sentences.zh: 「夫吳甡、鄭三俊，臣不謂無一事失，而端方諒直，終為海內正人之歸；

translations.literal: "As for Wu Shen and Zheng Sanjun, I do not say they never erred in anything, yet they are upright, sincere, and straightforward and in the end remain where the upright men of the empire look;
translations.idiomatic: "Wu Shen and Zheng Sanjun, I do not claim, never erred in a single matter, yet they are upright and sincere and in the end remain the refuge of the empire's honest men;

sentences.zh: 士英、大鋮，臣不謂無一技長，而奸回邪慝，終為宗社無窮之禍」。

translations.literal: as for Shiying and Dacheng, I do not say they lack a single skill, yet they are treacherous, perverse, and wicked and in the end are an unending calamity for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: as for Shiying and Dacheng, I do not deny they have some talent, yet they are treacherous and wicked and in the end are an endless disaster for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 疏入，以和衷體國答之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor answered that he should harmonize his heart with the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the throne answered that he should seek harmony and serve the state.

sentences.zh: 未幾，澤清入朝，劾大器、縯祚懷異圖。

translations.literal: Before long Zeqing entered court and impeached Daqi and Zuo for harboring ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zeqing came to court and impeached Daqi and Zuo for disloyal designs.

sentences.zh: 大器遂乞休去，以手書監國告廟文送內閣，明無他。

translations.literal: Daqi therefore asked to retire, sending by hand the regent's proclamation for temple sacrifice to the grand secretariat to show he had no other aim.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi then asked to retire, sending in his own hand the regent's temple proclamation to the grand secretariat to show he harbored no other intent.

sentences.zh: 士英憾未已，令太常少卿李沾劾之。

translations.literal: Shiying's resentment was not ended; he had the vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Zhan impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying's resentment was not spent; he had Li Zhan of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices impeach him.

sentences.zh: 遂削大器籍，復命法司逮治之。

translations.literal: Daqi's name was then struck from the registers and orders were again issued for the judicial offices to seize and try him.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi's name was struck from the registers and orders went out again for the judicial offices to arrest and try him.

sentences.zh: 以蜀地盡失，無可蹤跡而止。

translations.literal: Because Sichuan was wholly lost there was nowhere to trace him, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan was wholly lost and he could not be found, so the pursuit ended.

sentences.zh: 大器既去，沾得超擢左都御史。

translations.literal: After Daqi had gone, Zhan was abruptly promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Daqi left, Zhan was suddenly promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 謙益亦以附士英、大鋮，得為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Qianyi also, by attaching himself to Shiying and Dacheng, became minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi too, by siding with Shiying and Dacheng, became minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 獨縯祚論死。

translations.literal: Only Zuo was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zuo was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 明年，唐王召為兵部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: The following year the Prince of Tang summoned him as minister of War and grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Prince of Tang summoned him as minister of War and grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge.

sentences.zh: 道梗，久之至。

translations.literal: The routes were blocked and only after a long time did he arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were cut and only after a long delay did he arrive.

sentences.zh: 汀州失，奔廣東，與丁魁楚等擁永明王監國，令以原官兼掌兵部事。

translations.literal: When Tingzhou fell he fled to Guangdong and together with Ding Kuitai and others installed the Prince of Yongming as regent; he was ordered to hold his former office while additionally overseeing War.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhou fell he fled to Guangdong and with Ding Kuitai and others installed the Prince of Yongming as regent; he was ordered to keep his former office while also overseeing War.

sentences.zh: 久之，進少傅，盡督西南諸軍，代王應熊，賜劍，便宜從事。

translations.literal: After a time he was advanced to junior tutor, given complete command of the armies of the southwest in place of Wang Yingxiong, and granted the sword with authority to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to junior tutor, given full command of the southwestern armies in Wang Yingxiong's place, and granted the sword with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 至涪州，與將軍李占春深相結。

translations.literal: Reaching Fuzhou, he formed a deep bond with the general Li Zhanchun.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Fuzhou, he formed a close bond with the general Li Zhanchun.

sentences.zh: 他將楊展、於大海、胡雲風、袁韜、武大定、譚弘、譚詣、譚文以下，皆受大器約束。

translations.literal: The other generals Yang Zhan, Yu Dahai, Hu Yunfeng, Yuan Tao, Wu Dading, Tan Hong, Tan Yi, Tan Wen, and those below them all accepted Daqi's discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals Yang Zhan, Yu Dahai, Hu Yunfeng, Yuan Tao, Wu Dading, Tan Hong, Tan Yi, Tan Wen, and those below all submitted to Daqi's command.

sentences.zh: 宗室朱容藩自稱天下兵馬副元帥，據夔州。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Zhu Rongfan styled himself deputy supreme marshal of all troops under Heaven and held Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The clansman Zhu Rongfan styled himself deputy supreme marshal of all armies under Heaven and held Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大器檄占春、大海、雲風討殺容藩。

translations.literal: Daqi issued orders for Zhanchun, Dahai, and Yunfeng to attack and kill Rongfan.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi ordered Zhanchun, Dahai, and Yunfeng to attack and kill Rongfan.

sentences.zh: 大器至思南得疾，次都勻而卒，王謚為文肅。

translations.literal: Daqi fell ill at Sinan and died at the next stop in Duyun; the Prince gave him the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi fell ill at Sinan and died at Duyun on the way; the Prince granted the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 文安之

translations.literal: Wen Anzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wen Anzhi

sentences.zh: 文安之，夷陵人。

translations.literal: Wen Anzhi was a native of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Anzhi came from Yiling.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the second year of the Tianqi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the second year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討，除南京司業。

translations.literal: He was transferred to bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, appointed reviser, and removed to serve as vice director of studies at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor, appointed reviser, and transferred to vice director of studies at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，就遷祭酒，為薛國觀所構，削藉歸。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period he was promoted in place to director of the Directorate of Education but was framed by Xue Guoguan, stripped of rank, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he was promoted in place to director of the Directorate of Education, but Xue Guoguan framed him, stripped his rank, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 久之，言官交薦，未及召而京師陷。

translations.literal: After a long while the censorate officials recommended him in succession, but before he could be summoned the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval censors recommended him repeatedly, but before he could be summoned the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起為詹事。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was raised to grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was appointed grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 唐王復召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tang again summoned him and appointed him minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang summoned him again and made him minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 安之方轉側兵戈間，皆不赴。

translations.literal: Anzhi was then moving about amid the clash of arms and did not go to either post.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi was then adrift amid the fighting and went to neither post.

sentences.zh: 永明王以瞿式耜薦，與王錫兗並拜東閣大學士，亦不赴。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongming, on Qu Shisao's recommendation, appointed both him and Wang Xigun as grand secretaries of the Eastern Lodge, and again he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yongming, on Qu Shisao's recommendation, named him and Wang Xigun grand secretaries of the Eastern Lodge, and again he did not go.

sentences.zh: 順治七年六月，安之謁王梧州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Shunzhi, Anzhi called on the Prince at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Shunzhi, Anzhi visited the Prince at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 安之敦雅操，素淡宦情，遭國變，絕意用世。

translations.literal: Anzhi was cultivated and of lofty conduct, by nature indifferent to office; when the realm was overturned he utterly gave up hope of serving.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi was refined and upright, by nature cold to office; when the dynasty fell he utterly renounced public life.

sentences.zh: 至是見國勢愈危，慨然思起扶之，乃就職。

translations.literal: Now seeing the state more imperiled, he sighed and thought to rise to support it, and therefore took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Now seeing the realm more desperate, he sighed and resolved to rise and support it, and therefore took office.

sentences.zh: 時嚴起恒為首輔，王化澄、朱天麟次之，起恒讓安之而自處其下。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Qiheng was chief counselor, with Wang Huacheng and Zhu Tianlin below him; Qiheng yielded to Anzhi and placed himself beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qiheng was then chief counselor, with Wang Huacheng and Zhu Tianlin beneath; Qiheng yielded to Anzhi and ranked himself below.

sentences.zh: 孫可望再遣使乞封秦王，安之持不予。

translations.literal: Sun Keqi sent envoys again begging enfeoffment as Prince of Qin, and Anzhi steadfastly refused to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Keqi again sent envoys begging enfeoffment as Prince of Qin, and Anzhi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 其後桂林破，王奔南寧。

translations.literal: Afterward Guilin fell and the Prince fled to Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guilin fell and the Prince fled to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 大兵日迫，雲南又為可望據，不可往。

translations.literal: The Qing armies pressed daily closer, and Yunnan too was already held by Keqi, so there was nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: The northern armies pressed closer day by day, and Yunnan was already in Keqi's hands, so there was nowhere to flee.

sentences.zh: 安之念川中諸鎮兵尚強，欲結之，共獎王室，乃自請督師，加諸鎮封爵。

translations.literal: Anzhi considered that the garrison commanders of Sichuan still had strong forces and wished to unite with them and jointly uphold the royal house; he therefore volunteered to supervise the armies and add enfeoffments for the various commands.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi judged that the Sichuan garrisons were still strong and wished to join them in upholding the royal house; he therefore volunteered to supervise the armies and enfeoff the various commands.

sentences.zh: 王從之，加安之太子太保兼吏、兵二部尚書，總督川、湖諸處軍務，賜劍，便宜從事。

translations.literal: The Prince assented, promoted Anzhi to grand guardian of the heir apparent and concurrent minister of Personnel and War with overall command of military affairs in Sichuan, Huguang, and the surrounding districts, bestowed the sword with power to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince agreed, promoted Anzhi to grand guardian of the heir apparent and concurrent minister of Personnel and War with overall command in Sichuan, Huguang, and the rest, and granted the sword with discretionary power.

sentences.zh: 進諸將王光興，郝永忠、劉體仁、袁宗第、李來亨、王友進、塔天寶、馬雲翔、郝珍、李復榮、譚弘、譚詣、譚文、黨守素等公侯爵，即令安之賫敕印行。

translations.literal: The generals Wang Guangxing, Hao Yongzhong, Liu Tiren, Yuan Zongdi, Li Laiheng, Wang Youjin, Ta Tianbao, Ma Yunxiang, Hao Zhen, Li Furong, Tan Hong, Tan Yi, Tan Wen, Dang Shousu, and others were advanced to duke, marquis, and earl ranks, and Anzhi was at once ordered to convey the edicts and seals.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangxing, Hao Yongzhong, Liu Tiren, Yuan Zongdi, Li Laiheng, Wang Youjin, Ta Tianbao, Ma Yunxiang, Hao Zhen, Li Furong, Tan Hong, Tan Yi, Tan Wen, Dang Shousu, and others were raised to ducal, marquis, and earl ranks, and Anzhi was immediately ordered to carry the edicts and seals.

sentences.zh: 可望聞而惡之，又素銜前阻封議，遣兵伺於都勻，邀止安之，追奪光興等敕印。

translations.literal: When Keqi heard of this he was displeased, and bearing a long-standing grudge over the earlier blocked enfeoffment, he sent troops to lie in wait at Duyun, intercepted and stopped Anzhi, and pursued to seize the edicts and seals of Guangxing and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Keqi heard and was angered; nursing his old grudge over the blocked enfeoffment, he posted troops at Duyun, intercepted Anzhi, and pursued to seize Guangxing's edicts and seals.

sentences.zh: 留數月，乃令入湖廣。

translations.literal: After several months he at last allowed entry into Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Only after several months did he allow entry into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 安之遠客他鄉，無所歸，復赴貴州，將謁王於安龍。

translations.literal: Anzhi, a far wanderer in another man's land with nowhere to return, went again to Guizhou intending to call on the Prince at Anlong.
translations.idiomatic: A stranger far from home with nowhere to turn, Anzhi went again to Guizhou intending to visit the Prince at Anlong.

sentences.zh: 可望坐以罪，戍之畢節衛。

translations.literal: Keqi convicted him on a charge and banished him to the guard at Bijie.
translations.idiomatic: Keqi convicted him on a charge and banished him to the Bijie guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，可望欲設六部、翰林等官，慮人議其僭，乃以範礦、馬兆義、任僎、萬年策為吏、戶、禮、兵尚書，並加行營之號。

translations.literal: Earlier Keqi had wished to establish the Six Ministries and an Hanlin Academy and the like, fearing censure for usurpation; he therefore made Fan Kuang, Ma Zhaoyi, Ren Fu, and Wan Niance ministers of Personnel, Revenue, Rites, and War respectively, adding the designation of field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Keqi had wished to set up the Six Ministries and Hanlin Academy and the like, fearing charges of usurpation; he therefore made Fan Kuang, Ma Zhaoyi, Ren Fu, and Wan Niance ministers of Personnel, Revenue, Rites, and War, each with the added title of field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後又以程源代年策。

translations.literal: Later he replaced Niance with Cheng Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he replaced Niance with Cheng Yuan.

sentences.zh: 而僎最寵，與方於宣屢勸進，可望令待王入黔議之。

translations.literal: Fu was the most favored; together with Fang Yu'an he repeatedly urged Keqi to take the throne, and Keqi ordered them to wait until the Prince entered Guizhou to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was the most favored; with Fang Yu'an he repeatedly urged Keqi to ascend the throne, and Keqi told them to wait until the Prince entered Guizhou to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 王久駐安龍，可望遂自設內閣六部等官，以安之為東閣大學士。

translations.literal: The Prince had long been detained at Anlong, and Keqi thereupon set up his own inner court with the Six Ministries and the like, appointing Anzhi grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince had long been held at Anlong, and Keqi then established his own inner court and Six Ministries, making Anzhi grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge.

sentences.zh: 安之不為用，久之走川東，依劉體仁以居。

translations.literal: Anzhi would not serve him; after a long while he fled to eastern Sichuan and lived under Liu Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi refused to serve; in time he fled to eastern Sichuan and relied on Liu Tiren.

sentences.zh: 李赤心，高必正等久竄廣西賓、橫、南寧間。

translations.literal: Li Chixin, Gao Bizheng, and others had long been harried between Bin, Heng, and Nanning in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chixin, Gao Bizheng, and others had long lurked between Bin, Heng, and Nanning in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 赤心死，養子來亨代領其眾，推必正為主。

translations.literal: When Chixin died, his adopted son Laiheng took command of the host and they made Bizheng their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Chixin died, and his adopted son Laiheng led the band; they set Bizheng at their head.

sentences.zh: 必正又死，其眾食盡，且畏大兵逼，率眾走川東，分據川、湖間，耕田自給。

translations.literal: When Bizheng too died, their provisions were exhausted and, fearing the northern armies, they led the masses into eastern Sichuan, divided holdings between Sichuan and Huguang, and farmed to sustain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After Bizheng died as well, food ran out and, dreading the Qing advance, they marched into eastern Sichuan, held territory across Sichuan and Huguang, and farmed for their living.

sentences.zh: 川中舊將王光興、譚弘等附之，眾猶數十萬。

translations.literal: The old Sichuan commanders Wang Guangxing, Tan Hong, and others attached themselves to them, and their numbers still reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Former Sichuan generals such as Wang Guangxing and Tan Hong joined them, and their forces still numbered in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年正月，王奔永昌。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, the Prince fled to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Shunzhi 16 the Prince fled to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 安之率體仁、宗第、來亨等十六營由水道襲重慶。

translations.literal: Anzhi led Tiren, Zongdi, Laiheng, and sixteen camps by water to strike Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi led Tiren, Zongdi, Laiheng, and sixteen camps along the waterways against Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 會譚弘、譚詣殺譚文，諸將不服。

translations.literal: Just then Tan Hong and Tan Yi killed Tan Wen, and the generals would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Tan Hong and Tan Yi killed Tan Wen, and the commanders refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 安之欲討弘、詣，弘、詣懼，率所部降於大兵，諸鎮遂散。

translations.literal: Anzhi wished to punish Hong and Yi; in fear they led their troops to surrender to the Qing armies, and the garrisons scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi meant to punish Hong and Yi; terrified, they surrendered their commands to the Qing, and the garrisons broke up.

sentences.zh: 時王已入緬甸，地盡失，安之不久郁郁而卒。

translations.literal: By then the Prince had already entered Burma and the land was wholly lost; before long Anzhi died in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was already in Burma and the realm was gone; Anzhi soon died of grief.

sentences.zh: 樊一蘅

translations.literal: Fan Yiheng
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yiheng

sentences.zh: 樊一蘅，字君帶，宜賓人。

translations.literal: Fan Yiheng, styled Jundai, was a native of Yibin.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yiheng, whose style name was Jundai, came from Yibin.

sentences.zh: 父垣，常德知府。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was prefect of Changde.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan had been prefect of Changde.

sentences.zh: 一蘅舉萬歷四十七年進士，知安義、襄陽，累官吏部郎中，請告歸。

translations.literal: Yiheng passed the jinshi in the forty-seventh year of Wanli, served as magistrate of Anyi and Xiangyang, rose to director in the Ministry of Personnel, and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng took his jinshi in Wanli 47, governed Anyi and Xiangyang, became a director in the Ministry of Personnel, and sought leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年秋，遷榆林兵備參議。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Chongzhen he was transferred to military intendant of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of Chongzhen 3 he was made military intendant of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 流賊多榆林人，又久荒，饑民益相挻為盜。

translations.literal: Many of the roaming bandits were Yulin men, and the region had long lain waste, so hungry people increasingly incited one another to robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Many bandits were natives of Yulin, and the district had long been desolate; the hungry increasingly stirred one another to plunder.

sentences.zh: 一蘅撫創殘，修戎備，討斬申在庭、馬丙貴，平不沾泥。

translations.literal: Yiheng nursed the ravaged land, repaired defenses, campaigned against and beheaded Shen Zaiting and Ma Binggui, and pacified Bu Zhan Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng tended the ruined countryside, restored defenses, attacked and killed Shen Zaiting and Ma Binggui, and pacified Bu Zhan Ni.

sentences.zh: 累被薦，遷監軍副使，再遷右參政，分巡關南。

translations.literal: Repeatedly recommended, he was promoted to vice commissioner of military supervision, then to right assistant commissioner with circuit duty in Guannan.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended again and again, he became vice commissioner of military supervision, then right assistant commissioner patrolling Guannan.

sentences.zh: 總兵曹文詔敗歿，群賊迫西安。

translations.literal: When the regional commander Cao Wenchao was defeated and killed, the bandit hosts pressed on Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Cao Wenchao was defeated and killed, and the rebels closed on Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 總督洪承疇令一蘅監左光先、張應昌軍，連破賊，擊走混天星。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou ordered Yiheng to supervise the armies of Zuo Guangxian and Zhang Yingchang; they defeated the bandits in succession and drove off Huntianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou had Yiheng supervise Zuo Guangxian and Zhang Yingchang; they broke the rebels repeatedly and drove off Huntianxing.

sentences.zh: 賊逼漢中，瑞王告急，一蘅偕副將羅尚文往救。

translations.literal: When the bandits threatened Hanzhong, Prince Rui sent an urgent plea, and Yiheng went with Deputy General Luo Shangwen to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threatened Hanzhong and Prince Rui cried for help; Yiheng went with Deputy General Luo Shangwen to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 會承疇大軍至，賊乃走。

translations.literal: When Chengchou's main force arrived, the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou's great army came up and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 進按察使，偕副將馬科、賀人龍屢挫祁總管於漢中，降之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner and, with deputy generals Ma Ke and He Renlong, repeatedly routed Qi Zongguan at Hanzhong and accepted his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to surveillance commissioner, he with Ma Ke and He Renlong repeatedly crushed Qi Zongguan at Hanzhong and took his surrender.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢右僉都御史，代鄭崇儉巡撫寧夏，被劾罷歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was raised to right censor-in-chief to replace Zheng Chongjian as grand coordinator of Ningxia, was impeached, and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia in Zheng Chongjian's place, was impeached, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，用薦起兵部右侍郎，總督川、陜軍務，道阻，命不達。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year, on recommendation he was made right vice minister of War with overall command of Sichuan and Shaanxi military affairs, but the roads were blocked and the order never reached him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the sixteenth year he was recommended as right vice minister of War with overall command in Sichuan and Shaanxi, but the routes were cut and the appointment never arrived.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，福王立於南京，復申前命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing and the earlier order was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing and the earlier command was reissued.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠已據全蜀，惟遵義未陷，一蘅與王應熊避其地。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong had already seized all Shu; only Zunyi had not fallen, and Yiheng with Wang Yingxiong took refuge there.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong held all Shu; only Zunyi still stood, and Yiheng with Wang Yingxiong sheltered there.

sentences.zh: 既拜命，檄諸郡舊將會師大舉。

translations.literal: Once he received the commission, he issued proclamations summoning the old commanders of the prefectures to assemble for a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he summoned the former commanders of the districts to muster for a major offensive.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫馬乾復重慶，松潘副將朱化龍、同知詹天顏擊斬賊將王運行，復龍安、茂州。

translations.literal: Just then Grand Coordinator Ma Gan recovered Chongqing, and the deputy of Songpan Zhu Hualong with the subprefect Zhan Tianyan attacked and killed the rebel commander Wang Yunxing, recovering Long'an and Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ma Gan had just retaken Chongqing; Zhu Hualong of Songpan and Subprefect Zhan Tianyan killed the rebel Wang Yunxing and recovered Long'an and Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 一蘅乃起舊將甘良臣為總統，副以侯天錫、屠龍，合參將楊展，遊擊馬應試、余朝宗所攜潰卒，得三萬人。

translations.literal: Yiheng then raised the old general Gan Liangchen as supreme commander, with Hou Tianxi and Tu Long as deputies, and joined the routed troops brought by the battalion commanders Yang Zhan and the rangers Ma Yingshi and Yu Chaozong, mustering thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng made the old general Gan Liangchen supreme commander, with Hou Tianxi and Tu Long as deputies, and combined the broken bands of Yang Zhan, Ma Yingshi, and Yu Chaozong into thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 明年三月攻敘州，應試、朝宗先登，展等繼至，斬馘數千級。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year they attacked Xuzhou; Yingshi and Chaozong scaled first, Zhan and the rest followed, and several thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Next year in the third month they attacked Xuzhou; Yingshi and Chaozong led the assault, Zhan and others followed, and thousands were slain.

sentences.zh: 偽都督張化龍走，遂復其城。

translations.literal: The false regional commander Zhang Hualong fled, and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The false commander Zhang Hualong fled and the city was retaken.

sentences.zh: 一蘅乃犒師江上。

translations.literal: Yiheng then rewarded the army on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng then feasted the army on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 初，乾復重慶，賊將劉廷舉走，求救於獻忠。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gan recovered Chongqing, the rebel commander Liu Tingju fled and begged Xianzhong for aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan had retaken Chongqing, Liu Tingju fled and begged Xianzhong for help.

sentences.zh: 獻忠命養子劉文秀攻重慶，水陸並進。

translations.literal: Xianzhong ordered his adopted son Liu Wenxiu to attack Chongqing by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong sent his adopted son Liu Wenxiu against Chongqing by land and water.

sentences.zh: 副將曾英與參政劉麟長自遵義至，與部將於大海、李占春、張天相等夾擊，破賊兵數萬。

translations.literal: Deputy General Zeng Ying with the administrative commissioner Liu Linzhang came from Zunyi and, with the subordinates Yu Dahai, Li Zhanchun, and Zhang Tianxiang, attacked from both sides and broke tens of thousands of rebel troops.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy General Zeng Ying and Commissioner Liu Linzhang came from Zunyi and, with Yu Dahai, Li Zhanchun, and Zhang Tianxiang, struck from both sides and shattered tens of thousands of rebels.

sentences.zh: 英威名大振，諸別將皆屬，兵二十餘萬，奉一蘅節制。

translations.literal: Ying's fame rose greatly; the other detached commanders all submitted to him, and with more than two hundred thousand troops they obeyed Yiheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's renown soared; the other commanders attached themselves, and with more than two hundred thousand men they answered to Yiheng.

sentences.zh: 楊展既復敘州，賊將馮雙禮來寇，每戰輒敗，孫可望以大眾援之。

translations.literal: After Zhan had recovered Xuzhou, the rebel commander Feng Shuangli came to attack and was beaten in every battle; Sun Keqi brought a great host to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhan retook Xuzhou, Feng Shuangli attacked and was beaten each time; Sun Keqi came with a great army to aid him.

sentences.zh: 隔江持一月，糧盡，一蘅退屯古藺州，展退屯江津。

translations.literal: They faced one another across the river for a month; when provisions were exhausted, Yiheng withdrew to garrison at Gulian Prefecture and Zhan fell back to Jiangjin.
translations.idiomatic: For a month they held opposite banks until grain ran out; Yiheng withdrew to Gulian and Zhan to Jiangjin.

sentences.zh: 賊退截朱化龍及僉事蔡肱明於羊子嶺，化龍率番騎數百沖賊兵，賊驚潰，死者滿山谷。

translations.literal: As the rebels withdrew they cut off Zhu Hualong and the intendant Cai Gumeng at Yangzi Ridge; Hualong led several hundred tribal horsemen to charge the rebel line, and the rebels broke in panic with the dead filling the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels cut off Hualong and Intendant Cai Gumeng at Yangzi Ridge; Hualong charged with hundreds of tribal cavalry, the rebels fled in terror, and the valleys were heaped with dead.

sentences.zh: 化龍以軍孤，還守舊地。

translations.literal: Hualong, isolated, returned to hold his former ground.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong, alone, went back to his old post.

sentences.zh: 他將復連敗賊於摩泥、滴水。

translations.literal: Other commanders again defeated the rebels at Moni and Dishui.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals again beat the rebels at Moni and Dishui.

sentences.zh: 一蘅乃命展、應試取嘉定、邛、眉，故總兵官賈連登及其中軍楊維棟取資、簡，天錫、高明佐取瀘州，占春、大海守忠、涪。

translations.literal: Yiheng then ordered Zhan and Yingshi to take Jiazhou, Qiong, and Mei, the former regional commander Jia Liandeng and his chief officer Yang Weidong to take Zi and Jian, Tianxi and Gao Mingzuo to take Luzhou, and Zhanchun and Dahai to guard Zhong and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng ordered Zhan and Yingshi to take Jia, Qiong, and Mei; Jia Liandeng and Yang Weidong to take Zi and Jian; Tianxi and Gao Mingzuo Luzhou; Zhanchun and Dahai to hold Zhong and Fu.

sentences.zh: 其他據城邑奉征調者，洪、雅則曹勛及監軍副使範文光，松、茂則監軍僉事詹天顏，夔、萬則譚弘、譚詣。

translations.literal: Others holding cities who answered the call to arms were Cao Xun and the vice commissioner of military supervision Fan Wenguang at Hong and Ya, the military intendant Zhan Tianyan at Song and Mao, and Tan Hong and Tan Yi at Kui and Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held towns and answered the levy were Cao Xun and Fan Wenguang in Hong and Ya, Zhan Tianyan in Song and Mao, and Tan Hong and Tan Yi in Kui and Wan.

sentences.zh: 一蘅乃移駐納溪，居中調度，與督師應熊會瀘州，檄諸路刻欺並進。

translations.literal: Yiheng moved his headquarters to Naxi to direct affairs from the center; he met the supervising general Yingxiong at Luzhou and ordered every route to advance on a fixed day.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng moved to Naxi to direct operations, met Yingxiong at Luzhou, and ordered all columns to advance on a set day.

sentences.zh: 獻忠頗懼，盡屠境內民，沈金銀江中，大焚宮室，火連月不滅，將棄成都走川北。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was much afraid; he slaughtered the people throughout his territory, sank gold and silver in the river, burned palaces until fires burned for months without dying out, and prepared to abandon Chengdu for northern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was terrified; he massacred the people, sank treasure in the river, burned palaces for months, and meant to quit Chengdu for the north.

sentences.zh: 明年春，展盡取上川南地，屯嘉定，與勛等相聲援。

translations.literal: The next spring Zhan took all of upper southern Sichuan and camped at Jiazhou in mutual support with Xun and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Zhan seized upper south Sichuan and encamped at Jiazhou in concert with Xun and others.

sentences.zh: 而應熊及王祥在遵義，乾、英在重慶，皆宿重兵。

translations.literal: Yingxiong and Wang Xiang were at Zunyi, Gan and Ying at Chongqing, each with heavy garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong and Wang Xiang held Zunyi, Gan and Ying Chongqing, each with strong forces.

sentences.zh: 賊勢日蹙，惟保寧、順慶為賊將劉進忠所守，進忠又數敗。

translations.literal: The rebels' plight tightened daily; only Baoning and Shunqing were held by the rebel commander Liu Jinzhong, and Jinzhong too had suffered many defeats.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew desperate; only Baoning and Shunqing remained under Liu Jinzhong, who had himself been beaten repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 獻忠怒，遣孫可望、劉文秀、王尚禮、狄三品、王復臣等攻川南郡縣。

translations.literal: Xianzhong in anger sent Sun Keqi, Liu Wenxiu, Wang Shangli, Di Sanpin, Wang Fuchen, and others to attack the prefectures and counties of southern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In rage Xianzhong sent Keqi, Wenxiu, Wang Shangli, Di Sanpin, Wang Fuchen, and others against south Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 應熊、一蘅急令展、天錫、龍、應試及顧存誌、莫宗文、張登貴連營犍為、敘州以禦之。

translations.literal: Yingxiong and Yiheng urgently ordered Zhan, Tianxi, Long, Yingshi, Gu Cunzhi, Mo Zongwen, and Zhang Denggui to camp at Qianwei and Xuzhou to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong and Yiheng ordered Zhan, Tianxi, Long, Yingshi, Gu Cunzhi, Mo Zongwen, and Zhang Denggui to encamp at Qianwei and Xuzhou to meet them.

sentences.zh: 賊連戰不利，英、祥乘間趨成都，獻忠立召可望等還。

translations.literal: The rebels lost battle after battle; Ying and Xiang seized the chance to press toward Chengdu, and Xianzhong at once recalled Keqi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lost again and again; Ying and Xiang pressed on Chengdu, and Xianzhong recalled Keqi and his commanders.

sentences.zh: 又聞大清兵入蜀境，劉進忠降，大懼。

translations.literal: He also heard that Qing troops had entered the Shu border; Liu Jinzhong surrendered, and he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Qing armies had entered Shu; Jinzhong surrendered, and he was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 七月，棄成都走順慶，尋入西充之風凰山。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he abandoned Chengdu for Shunqing and soon entered Fenghuang Mountain in Xichong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he fled Chengdu for Shunqing and soon entered Fenghuang Mountain in Xichong.

sentences.zh: 至十二月，大清兵奄至，射殺獻忠，賊降及敗死者二三十萬。

translations.literal: By the twelfth month Qing troops came suddenly, shot Xianzhong dead, and rebels who surrendered or were killed numbered two or three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth month Qing forces arrived, shot Xianzhong dead, and two or three hundred thousand rebels surrendered or perished.

sentences.zh: 可望等率殘卒南奔，驟至重慶。

translations.literal: Keqi and the others led the remnant south in flight and suddenly reached Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Keqi and the rest fled south with the remnant and suddenly appeared at Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 英出不意，戰敗，死於江。

translations.literal: Ying, taken unawares, was defeated and died in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, caught unprepared, was beaten and died in the river.

sentences.zh: 賊遂陷綦江，應熊避之畢節衛。

translations.literal: The rebels then took Qijiang, and Yingxiong fled to the Bijie guard.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Qijiang and Yingxiong fled to the Bijie guard.

sentences.zh: 逾月，賊陷遵義，入貴州。

translations.literal: A month later they took Zunyi and entered Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A month later they seized Zunyi and entered Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 大清兵追至重慶，巡撫乾敗死，遂入遵義。

translations.literal: Qing troops pursued to Chongqing; Grand Coordinator Gan was defeated and killed, and they entered Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Qing pursuers reached Chongqing; Gan was defeated and killed, and they entered Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 以餉乏，旋師。

translations.literal: Supplies ran short and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking provisions, they turned back.

sentences.zh: 王祥等復取保、寧二郡。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang and others again recovered the two prefectures of Bao and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang and others retook Bao and Ning.

sentences.zh: 一蘅再駐江上，為收復全蜀計，乃列上善後事宜及諸將功狀於永明王。

translations.literal: Yiheng again encamped on the river planning the recovery of all Shu and memorialized the Prince of Yongming with plans for pacification and the merits of the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng again held the river line, planning to recover all Shu, and sent the Prince of Yongming his pacification plans and a roll of the generals' merits.

sentences.zh: 拜一蘅戶、兵二部尚書，加太子太傅，祥、展、天錫等進爵有差。

translations.literal: Yiheng was made concurrent minister of Revenue and War, promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent, and Xiang, Zhan, Tianxi, and others were advanced in rank by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng was made minister of Revenue and War, raised to grand tutor of the heir apparent, and Xiang, Zhan, Tianxi, and others were ennobled in turn.

sentences.zh: 時應熊已卒，而宗室朱容藩、故偏沅巡撫李乾德並以總制至，楊喬然、江爾文以巡撫至，各自署置，官多於民。

translations.literal: Yingxiong had already died, while the clansman Zhu Rongfan and the former grand coordinator of Bian Yuan Li Qiande both arrived claiming overall command, and Yang Qiaoran and Jiang Erwen came as grand coordinators, each appointing officials until offices outnumbered the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong was dead; Zhu Rongfan and the former Bian Yuan coordinator Li Qiande arrived as supreme commanders; Yang Qiaoran and Jiang Erwen came as grand coordinators—each created posts until officials outnumbered the people.

sentences.zh: 諸將袁韜據重慶，於大海據雲陽，李占春據涪州，譚詣據巫山，譚文據萬縣，譚弘據天字城，侯天錫據永寧，馬應試據蘆衛，王祥據遵義，楊展據嘉定，朱化龍、曹勛仍據故地。

translations.literal: General Yuan Tao held Chongqing, Yu Dahai Yunyang, Li Zhanchun Fuzhou, Tan Yi Wushan, Tan Wen Wanxian, Tan Hong Tianzi City, Hou Tianxi Yongning, Ma Yingshi Lusi guard, Wang Xiang Zunyi, Yang Zhan Jiazhou, and Zhu Hualong and Cao Xun their former territories.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tao held Chongqing, Yu Dahai Yunyang, Li Zhanchun Fuzhou, Tan Yi Wushan, Tan Wen Wanxian, Tan Hong Tianzi City, Hou Tianxi Yongning, Ma Yingshi the Lusi guard, Wang Xiang Zunyi, Yang Zhan Jiazhou, Zhu Hualong and Cao Xun their old lands.

sentences.zh: 搖、黃諸家據夔州夾江兩岸，而李自成餘孽李赤心等十三家亦在建始縣。

translations.literal: The Yao and Huang families held both banks of the Jia River in Kui Prefecture, and the thirteen bands of Li Chixin's remnant from Li Zicheng also lay in Jianshi County.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao and Huang clans held both banks of the Jia in Kui, and thirteen bands of Li Zicheng's remnant under Li Chixin were in Jianshi.

sentences.zh: 一蘅令不行，保敘州一郡而已。

translations.literal: Yiheng's orders went unheeded; he held only the single prefecture of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng could command nothing; only Xuzhou obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，容藩自稱楚世子，建行臺夔州，稱制封拜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi Rongfan styled himself heir of Chu, set up a field headquarters at Kui Prefecture, and assumed the power to enfeoff and appoint.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 Rongfan called himself heir of Chu, established a headquarters at Kui, and enfeoffed and appointed at will.

sentences.zh: 時喬然已進總督，而範文光、詹天顏巡撫川南、北，呂大器以大學士來督師，皆惡容藩，謀誅之。

translations.literal: Qiaoran had already been made grand coordinator, while Fan Wenguang and Zhan Tianyan were grand coordinators of south and north Sichuan and Lu Daqi came as grand secretary to supervise the armies; all hated Rongfan and plotted his death.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaoran was grand coordinator; Fan Wenguang and Zhan Tianyan governed south and north Sichuan; Lu Daqi came as grand secretary to supervise the armies—all detested Rongfan and plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 六年春，容藩遂為占春所敗，走死雲陽。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Rongfan was defeated by Zhanchun and fled to die at Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the sixth year Zhanchun defeated Rongfan, who fled and died at Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 初，展與祥有隙，遣子璟新攻之。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhan and Xiang had been at odds; Zhan sent his son Jingxin to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and Xiang had quarreled; Zhan sent his son Jingxin against him.

sentences.zh: 璟新先襲殺應試，與祥戰敗歸。

translations.literal: Jingxin first made a surprise attack and killed Yingshi, fought Xiang, was beaten, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxin ambushed and killed Yingshi, fought Xiang, lost, and came back.

sentences.zh: 乾德利展富，說韜、大定殺展，分其貲。

translations.literal: Qiande, coveting Zhan's wealth, persuaded Tao and Dading to kill Zhan and divide his goods.
translations.idiomatic: Qiande, greedy for Zhan's wealth, incited Tao and Dading to murder Zhan and share his property.

sentences.zh: 一蘅誚乾德，諸鎮亦皆憤，有離心。

translations.literal: Yiheng reproached Qiande, and the garrisons were all angry and lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng rebuked Qiande; the commands were furious and lost cohesion.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，孫可望遣白文選攻殺祥，降其眾二十餘萬，盡得遵義、重慶。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Sun Keqi sent Bai Wenxuan to attack and kill Xiang, accepting the surrender of more than two hundred thousand of his troops and taking Zunyi and Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Keqi sent Bai Wenxuan to kill Xiang, take the surrender of two hundred thousand men, and seize Zunyi and Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 一蘅益孤。

translations.literal: Yiheng was more isolated than ever.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng stood alone as never before.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，可望又使劉文秀大敗武大定兵，長驅至嘉定。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year Keqi again sent Liu Wenxiu to rout Wu Dading's army and drive straight to Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the seventh year Keqi sent Wenxiu to crush Wu Dading and march on Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 大定、韜皆降，乾德投水死。

translations.literal: Dading and Tao both surrendered, and Qiande drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dading and Tao surrendered; Qiande threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 文秀兵復東，譚弘、譚詣、譚文盡降。

translations.literal: Wenxiu's army turned east; Tan Hong, Tan Yi, and Tan Wen all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu marched east; Tan Hong, Tan Yi, and Tan Wen all submitted.

sentences.zh: 占春、大海降於大清。

translations.literal: Zhanchun and Dahai surrendered to the Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanchun and Dahai went over to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，文秀還雲南，留文選守嘉定，劉鎮國守雅州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Wenxiu returned to Yunnan, leaving Wenxuan to hold Jiazhou and Liu Zhenguo to hold Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Next year in the first month Wenxiu returned to Yunnan, leaving Wenxuan at Jiazhou and Liu Zhenguo at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，大清兵南征，文選、鎮國挾曹勛走，文光、天顏、化龍相繼死。

translations.literal: In the third month Qing armies marched south; Wenxuan and Zhenguo took Cao Xun and fled, and Wenguang, Tianyan, and Hualong died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Qing advanced south; Wenxuan and Zhenguo fled with Cao Xun, and Wenguang, Tianyan, and Hualong died one after another.

sentences.zh: 一蘅時已謝事，避山中。

translations.literal: Yiheng had already retired and hid in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng had resigned and hidden in the hills.

sentences.zh: 至九月，亦遘疾死。

translations.literal: By the ninth month he too fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month he too fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 文武將吏盡亡。

translations.literal: Civil and military officers and men were wholly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military leaders were all gone.

sentences.zh: 范文光

translations.literal: Fan Wenguang
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenguang

sentences.zh: 范文光，內江人。

translations.literal: Fan Wenguang was a native of Neijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenguang came from Neijiang.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the early Tianqi period he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，歷官工部主事，南京戶部員外郎，告歸。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period he served as director in the Ministry of Works, as assistant department director of Revenue at Nanjing, and asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he was a director in Works, an assistant director of Revenue at Nanjing, then went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 十七年，張獻忠亂蜀，文光偕邛州舉人劉道貞，蘆山舉人程翔風，雅州諸生傅元修、洪其仁等舉義兵，奉鎮國將軍朱平檙為蜀王，推黎州參將曹勛為副總兵，統諸將，而文光以副使為監軍，道貞等授官有差。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Zhang Xianzhong ravaged Shu, Wenguang with the provincial graduate Liu Daozhen of Qiongzhou, the graduate Cheng Xiangfeng of Lushan, and the students Fu Yuanxiu and Hong Qiren of Yazhou and others raised righteous troops, installed the Defender of the State General Zhu Pingcheng as Prince of Shu, made the assistant commander of Lizhou Cao Xun vice commander-in-chief to command the generals, and Wenguang served as military intendant with the rank of vice commissioner while Daozhen and the rest received offices by rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when Xianzhong ravaged Shu, Wenguang with Liu Daozhen of Qiong, Cheng Xiangfeng of Lushan, Fu Yuanxiu and Hong Qiren of Ya, and others raised loyalist forces, set up General Zhu Pingcheng as Prince of Shu, made Lizhou's Cao Xun vice commander over the generals, and Wenguang served as supervising vice commissioner while the rest were given posts.

sentences.zh: 勛敗賊雅州龍鸛山，追至城下，反為所敗，退守小關山。

translations.literal: Xun defeated the rebels at Longyan Mountain in Yazhou and pursued them to the walls, but was in turn defeated and fell back to hold Xiaoguanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun beat the rebels at Longyan Mountain in Ya and pursued to the walls, but was beaten in turn and withdrew to Xiaoguanshan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，文光督參將黎神武攻雅州，不克。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Wenguang supervised Battalion Commander Li Shenwu in attacking Yazhou without success.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wenguang led Li Shenwu against Yazhou without success.

sentences.zh: 明年九月，神武合雅州土、漢兵再擊賊將艾能奇於雅州，敗績。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year Shenwu with the native and Han troops of Yazhou again attacked the rebel Ai Nengqi at Yazhou and was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Next year in the ninth month Shenwu with Ya's tribal and Han troops again struck Ai Nengqi at Ya and was routed.

sentences.zh: 偽監司郝孟旋守錦州，文光、翔鳳遣間使招之，孟旋襲殺守雅州賊，以城來歸，文光等入居之。

translations.literal: The false intendant Hao Mengxuan held Jinzhou; Wenguang and Xiangfeng sent secret agents to win him over, and Mengxuan made a surprise attack, killed the garrison at Yazhou, and surrendered the city; Wenguang and the rest entered and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: The false intendant Hao Mengxuan held Jin; Wenguang and Xiangfeng sent agents to win him; Mengxuan surprised the Ya garrison, killed them, and offered the city; Wenguang entered and held it.

sentences.zh: 獻忠死，文光保境如故。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong died, Wenguang kept his territory as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhong died, Wenguang held his ground unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永明王命為右僉都御史，巡撫川南，而以安綿道詹天顏巡撫川北。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongming appointed him right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of southern Sichuan, with the Anmian circuit intendant Zhan Tianyan as grand coordinator of northern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yongming made him right censor-in-chief governing south Sichuan, with Zhan Tianyan governing the north.

sentences.zh: 總督李乾德殺楊展，文光惡之，遂入山不視事。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Li Qiande killed Yang Zhan; Wenguang detested this and withdrew to the mountains and ignored his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinator Li Qiande killed Yang Zhan; Wenguang loathed it, retired to the hills, and ceased to govern.

sentences.zh: 大清兵克嘉定，文光賦詩一章，仰藥死。

translations.literal: When Qing troops took Jiazhou, Wenguang composed a poem, took poison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing took Jiazhou, Wenguang wrote a poem, took poison, and died.

sentences.zh: 天顏兵敗被執，亦死之。

translations.literal: Tianyan was defeated and captured and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyan was beaten, taken prisoner, and likewise met his death.

sentences.zh: 天顏，龍巖人，起家選貢生。

translations.literal: Tianyan was a native of Longyan who began his career as a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyan came from Longyan and entered service as a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 吳炳，宜興人。

translations.literal: Wu Bing was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bing came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi at the end of the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi at the end of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授蒲圻知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，歷官江西提學副使。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period he served as vice education intendant of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he was vice education intendant of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 江西地盡失，流寓廣東。

translations.literal: Jiangxi was wholly lost and he took refuge in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi fell he fled to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 永明王擢為兵部右侍郎，從至桂林，令以本官兼東閣大學士，仍掌部事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongming promoted him to right vice minister of War; he followed to Guilin and was ordered to serve as grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge in his existing office while still overseeing the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yongming made him right vice minister of War; he went to Guilin and was ordered to be grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge while retaining the ministry.

sentences.zh: 又從至武岡。

translations.literal: He again followed to Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed again to Wugang.

sentences.zh: 大兵至，王倉猝奔靖州，令炳扈王太子走城步，吏部主事侯偉時從之。

translations.literal: When the northern armies arrived, the Prince fled in haste to Jingzhou and ordered Bing to escort the crown prince to Chengbu, with the director in the Ministry of Personnel Hou Weishi accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing armies came and the Prince fled headlong to Jingzhou, ordering Bing to escort the crown prince to Chengbu with Hou Weishi of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 既至，城已為大兵所據，遂被執，送衡州。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the city had already been taken by the northern armies; they were seized and sent to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengbu was already in enemy hands; they were captured and sent to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 炳不食，自盡於湘山寺，偉時亦死之。

translations.literal: Bing refused food and killed himself at Xiangshan Temple; Weishi also died.
translations.idiomatic: Bing starved himself to death at Xiangshan Temple, and Weishi died as well.

sentences.zh: 偉時，公安人。

translations.literal: Weishi was a native of Gongan.
translations.idiomatic: Weishi came from Gongan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中進士，歷官吏部考功主事，罷官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the Chongzhen period and served as director of the Merit Evaluation Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel before dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He was a Chongzhen jinshi, served as director of the Merit Evaluation Bureau, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 至是補官數月，即遘難。

translations.literal: He had held office again for only a few months when he met this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He had been restored to office only a few months when disaster struck.

sentences.zh: 王錫袞

translations.literal: Wang Xigun
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xigun

sentences.zh: 王錫袞，祿豐人。

translations.literal: Wang Xigun was a native of Lufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xigun came from Lufeng.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Tianqi 2.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin bachelor and reviser.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，累官少詹事。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period he rose to junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he rose to junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 十三年擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to right vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made right vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，尚書林欲楫出視孝陵，錫袞以左侍郎掌部事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the following year, when Minister Lin Yuqi went out to inspect the Xiaoling tomb, Xigun as left vice minister directed the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Next autumn Minister Lin Yuqi inspected the imperial tombs and Xigun, as left vice minister, ran the ministry.

sentences.zh: 帝禁內臣干預外政，敕禮官稽先朝典制以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor forbade inner eunuchs to interfere in outer government and ordered the rites officials to investigate earlier-dynasty regulations and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor barred inner eunuchs from outer politics and ordered the rites officials to report on earlier regulations.

sentences.zh: 錫袞等備列諸監局職掌，而不及東廠。

translations.literal: Xigun and the others fully listed the duties of the various directorates and offices but did not mention the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Xigun and his colleagues listed every directorate and office but omitted the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 提督內臣王德化言：「東廠之設，始永樂十八年，《國朝典匯》可據。

translations.literal: The supervising inner eunuch Wang Dehua said: "The Eastern Depot was established in the eighteenth year of Yongle; the Dynastic Regulations of Our Court can be cited."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising eunuch Wang Dehua said: "The Eastern Depot was founded in Yongle 18; the court regulations attest it."

sentences.zh: 禮官覆議不及，請解臣職，停廠不設。

translations.literal: The rites officials replied that they had not covered it in their review and asked to be relieved and the depot abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The rites officials answered that they had omitted it and asked to resign and have the depot shut.

sentences.zh: 」錫袞等言：「《典匯》雖載此條，但系下文箋註。

translations.literal: "Xigun and the others said: "Although the Regulations record this entry, it is only a marginal note below the text."
translations.idiomatic: Xigun replied: "The Regulations mention it, but only as a marginal gloss."

sentences.zh: 臣等以正史無文，故不敢妾引。

translations.literal: "We dared not cite it without authority in the standard histories."
translations.idiomatic: "We had no warrant in the standard histories and dared not cite it."

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 錫袞復抗疏，請罷廠，亦不允。

translations.literal: Xigun again memorialized urgently asking that the depot be abolished, and again it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xigun memorialized again to abolish the depot and was again refused.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝再耕耤田。

translations.literal: In the second month the emperor again plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor plowed the sacred field again.

sentences.zh: 錫袞因言頻歲旱蝗，三餉疊派，請量除加征，嚴核蠹餉，俾農夫樂生。

translations.literal: Xigun spoke of successive years of drought and locusts and the triple levies piled on one another, asking that the extra surcharges be reduced and corrupt military pay strictly audited so farmers could live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He cited drought, locusts, and triple levies, asking that surcharges be cut and corrupt military funds audited so farmers might live.

sentences.zh: 又以時方急才，請召還故侍郎陳子壯、顧錫疇，故祭酒倪元璐、文安之，且乞免黃道周永戍。

translations.literal: Because talent was urgently needed, he asked to recall the former vice ministers Chen Zizhuang and Gu Xichou, the former directors of the Directorate Ni Yuanlu and Wen Anzhi, and to lift Huang Daozhou's lifelong banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recall Chen Zizhuang, Gu Xichou, Ni Yuanlu, and Wen Anzhi and to end Huang Daozhou's exile.

sentences.zh: 給事中沈胤培請增天下解額，錫袞因言南畿、浙江人文更盛，宜倍增。

translations.literal: When the supervising secretary Shen Yinpei asked to increase the provincial quota nationwide, Xigun said that the southern capital region and Zhejiang were even richer in talent and should be doubled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Yinpei sought higher provincial quotas, Xigun urged doubling them for the southern capital and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 又言舉人不第，有三十年不謁選者，宜定制。

translations.literal: He also said that provincial graduates who failed the metropolitan examination sometimes went thirty years without presenting themselves for appointment and that a rule should be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: He noted graduates who failed the palace exam might wait thirty years for office and asked for a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 數科不售，即令服官。

translations.literal: After several failures without success they should be ordered to take office.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated failure they should be required to serve.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 欲楫還朝，錫袞調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Yuqi returned to court, Xigun was transferred to minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqi returned and Xigun became minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 李日宣下獄，遂掌部事。

translations.literal: Li Rixuan was imprisoned and Xigun thereupon directed the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rixuan was imprisoned and Xigun directed the ministry.

sentences.zh: 帝性純孝，嘗以秋夜感念聖母孝純太后，遂欲終身蔬食。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply filial by nature; one autumn night, moved by thoughts of his mother Empress Dowager Xiaochun, he wished to eat only vegetables for life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply filial; one autumn night, remembering Empress Dowager Xiaochun, he wished to eat only vegetables forever.

sentences.zh: 錫袞疏諫，帝嘉其寓愛於規，進秩一等。

translations.literal: Xigun remonstrated in a memorial; the emperor praised him for lodging love within counsel and raised his rank one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Xigun remonstrated; the emperor praised his loving counsel and raised his rank.

sentences.zh: 尋解部務，直講筵。

translations.literal: Soon he left the ministry and lectured at the classics mat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left the ministry to lecture at court.

sentences.zh: 十六年憂歸。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he retired for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he went home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 唐王立，拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang was enthroned, Xigun was made minister of Rites and grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang made him minister of Rites and Eastern Lodge grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 永明王立，申前命。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yongming was enthroned, the earlier appointment was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yongming renewed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 皆不至。

translations.literal: He went to neither.
translations.idiomatic: He answered neither summons.

sentences.zh: 土酋沙定洲作亂，執至會城，詭草錫袞疏上永明王，言定洲忠勇，請代黔國公鎮雲南。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Sha Dingzhou rebelled, seized him at the provincial capital, and forged a memorial in Xigun's name to the Prince of Yongming saying Dingzhou was loyal and brave and should replace the Duke of Qian in governing Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Sha Dingzhou rebelled, seized him, and forged a memorial in his name praising Dingzhou and asking that he replace the Duke of Qian in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 疏既行，以稿示之。

translations.literal: After the memorial was sent, he showed Xigun the draft.
translations.idiomatic: After sending it he showed Xigun the draft.

sentences.zh: 錫袞大恨，訴上帝祈死。

translations.literal: Xigun hated this deeply and prayed to God for death.
translations.idiomatic: Xigun was filled with hatred and prayed Heaven for death.

sentences.zh: 居數日，竟卒。

translations.literal: Within a few days he died at last.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he died.

sentences.zh: 堵胤錫

translations.literal: Du Yinxi
translations.idiomatic: Du Yinxi

sentences.zh: 堵胤錫，字仲緘，無錫人。

translations.literal: Du Yinxi, styled Zhongjian, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yinxi, style name Zhongjian, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the tenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Chongzhen 10.

sentences.zh: 歷官長沙知府。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He was prefect of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 山賊掠安化、寧鄉，官軍數敗，胤錫督鄉兵破滅之，又殺醴陵賊魁，遂以知兵名。

translations.literal: When mountain bandits raided Anhua and Ningxiang and government troops were repeatedly beaten, Yinxi led local militia to destroy them and also killed the bandit chief of Liling, and thus gained a reputation for knowing warfare.
translations.idiomatic: When mountain bandits ravaged Anhua and Ningxiang and official troops lost repeatedly, Yinxi led militia to destroy them, killed the Liling chief, and won fame as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 十六年八月，賊陷長沙。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year bandits took Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year rebels took Changsha.

sentences.zh: 胤錫朝覲還，賊已退。

translations.literal: Yinxi returned from court audience and the bandits had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi returned from audience and the rebels had already left.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，福王命為湖廣參政，分守武昌、黃州、漢陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year the Prince of Fu appointed him assistant administrator of Huguang with defense of Wuchang, Huangzhou, and Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Next year in the sixth month the Prince of Fu made him Huguang administrator defending Wuchang, Huangzhou, and Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 左良玉稱兵，總督何騰蛟奔長沙，令攝湖北巡撫事，駐常德。

translations.literal: When Zuo Liangyu raised troops, Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao fled to Changsha and ordered Yinxi to act as Hubei grand coordinator, stationing at Changde.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo Liangyu mutinied, He Tengjiao fled to Changsha and had Yinxi act as Hubei grand coordinator at Changde.

sentences.zh: 唐王立，拜右副都御史，實授巡撫。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang was enthroned, Yinxi was made right vice censor-in-chief and formally appointed grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang made him right vice censor-in-chief and confirmed him as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 李自成死，眾擁其兄子錦為主，奉自成妻高氏及高氏弟一功，驟至澧州。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng died the masses set up his elder brother's son Jin as leader, with Zicheng's wife Lady Gao and her brother Yigong, and they suddenly reached Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Zicheng died his nephew Jin was made leader with Lady Gao and her brother Yigong, and they suddenly reached Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 擁眾三十萬，言乞降，遠近大震。

translations.literal: With three hundred thousand followers they asked to surrender, and near and far were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: With three hundred thousand men they begged to surrender and the region was terrified.

sentences.zh: 胤錫議撫之，騰蛟亦馳檄至。

translations.literal: Yinxi favored pacification and Tengjiao also sent urgent orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi favored pacification and Tengjiao sent urgent orders as well.

sentences.zh: 乃躬入其營，開誠慰諭，稱詔賜高氏命服，錦、一功蟒玉金銀器，犒其軍，皆踴躍拜謝。

translations.literal: He then entered their camp in person, spoke frankly to comfort them, announced imperial gifts of court robes for Lady Gao and python robes, jade, gold, and silver for Jin and Yigong, and rewarded the army; all leaped up in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He entered their camp, spoke openly, bestowed court robes on Lady Gao and regalia on Jin and Yigong, feasted the army, and all bowed in joy.

sentences.zh: 乃即軍中宴之，導以忠孝大義數千言。

translations.literal: He then feasted them in camp and instructed them in the great principles of loyalty and filial piety in several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted them in camp and preached loyalty and filial piety at length.

sentences.zh: 明日，高氏出拜，謂錦曰：「堵公，天人也，汝不可負！

translations.literal: The next day Lady Gao came out to bow and said to Jin: "Master Du is a man of Heaven; you must not betray him!
translations.idiomatic: Next day Lady Gao bowed and told Jin: "Master Du is heaven-sent; you must not betray him!

sentences.zh: 」別部田見秀、劉汝魁等亦來歸。

translations.literal: "Other divisions such as Tian Jianxiu and Liu Rukui also came over.
translations.idiomatic: "Tian Jianxiu, Liu Rukui, and other bands also submitted.

sentences.zh: 唐王大喜，加胤錫兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總制其軍，手書獎勞。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tang was greatly pleased, promoted Yinxi to right vice minister of War and right censor-in-chief with overall command of the army, and wrote him a letter of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang rejoiced, made Yinxi right vice minister of War and right censor-in-chief commanding the army, and wrote to praise him.

sentences.zh: 授錦禦營前部左軍，一功右軍，並掛龍虎將軍印，封列侯。

translations.literal: Jin was made left army of the forward division of the Imperial Camp, Yigong the right army, each bearing the seal of Dragon-Tiger General and enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was made left army of the Imperial Camp vanguard, Yigong the right, each with the Dragon-Tiger seal and a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 賜錦名赤心，一功名必正，他部賞賚有差，號其營曰忠貞。

translations.literal: Jin was given the name Chixin, Yigong the name Bizheng, other units were rewarded in turn, and their camp was styled Loyal and Steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was renamed Chixin, Yigong Bizheng, other bands were rewarded, and the camp was called Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 封高氏貞義夫人，賜珠冠彩幣，命有司建坊，題曰：「淑贊中興」。

translations.literal: Lady Gao was enfeoffed as Lady of Chaste Righteousness, given a pearl crown and colored silks, and ordered that a memorial arch be built inscribed "Virtue aiding restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao became Lady of Chaste Righteousness, received crown and silks, and an arch was raised: "Virtue aiding restoration."

sentences.zh: 胤錫遂與赤心等深相結，倚以自強。

translations.literal: Yinxi then formed a deep bond with Chixin and relied on them to strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi bonded closely with Chixin and leaned on them for strength.

sentences.zh: 然赤心書疏猶稱自成先帝，稱高氏太后云。

translations.literal: Yet in his letters Chixin still called Zicheng "former emperor" and Lady Gao "empress dowager."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chixin's letters still called Zicheng "former emperor" and Lady Gao "empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 已而袁宗第、劉體仁諸營先歸騰蛟者，亦引與赤心合，眾益盛。
