translations.literal: Before long Yuan Zongdi, Liu Tiren, and other camps that had earlier submitted to Tengjiao were also joined with Chixin, and their numbers grew greater.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Zongdi, Liu Tiren, and other camps under Tengjiao merged with Chixin and swelled.

sentences.zh: 胤錫以芻糧難繼，令散處江北就食。

translations.literal: Yinxi, finding fodder hard to supply, ordered them dispersed north of the river to forage.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder failing, Yinxi sent them north of the river to live off the land.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，騰蛟大舉，期諸軍盡會岳州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Tengjiao launched a great campaign, fixing a day for all armies to assemble at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Next year in the first month Tengjiao launched a great offensive, summoning all armies to Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 獨赤心先至，餘逗遛，卒不進。

translations.literal: Only Chixin arrived first; the rest lingered and in the end did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chixin came first; the rest dallied and never advanced.

sentences.zh: 永明王立，進胤錫兵部尚書，總制如故。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yongming was enthroned, Yinxi was promoted to minister of War with his overall command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yongming promoted Yinxi to minister of War with command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，永明王令赤心等攻荊州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi the Prince of Yongming ordered Chixin and the rest to attack Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 the Prince ordered Chixin to attack Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 月餘，大清兵援荊州。

translations.literal: After more than a month Qing armies relieved Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a month Qing forces relieved the city.

sentences.zh: 赤心等大敗，步走入蜀，數日不得食。

translations.literal: Chixin and the others were heavily defeated, fled on foot into Shu, and for days had nothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Chixin was routed, fled on foot into Shu, and went days without food.

sentences.zh: 乃散入施州衛，聲言就食湖南。

translations.literal: They then scattered into Shizhou guard, claiming they would forage in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: They scattered into Shizhou guard, saying they would forage in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時王在武岡，劉承胤懼為赤心所並，計非胤錫不能禦，乃加胤錫東閣大學士，封光化伯，賜劍，便宜從事。

translations.literal: The Prince was then at Wugang; Liu Chengyin feared being absorbed by Chixin and judged only Yinxi could check them, so Yinxi was made Eastern Lodge grand secretary, enfeoffed as Baron of Guanghua, granted the sword with discretionary power.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was at Wugang; Liu Chengyin feared Chixin and made Yinxi grand secretary, Baron of Guanghua, with the sword.

sentences.zh: 胤錫疏請得給空敕鑄印，頒賜秦中舉兵者，時頗議其專。

translations.literal: Yinxi memorialized asking blank commissions and seals to bestow on those raising troops in Qin, and at the time many criticized his overreach.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi asked for blank commissions and seals for Qin rebels, drawing criticism of his power.

sentences.zh: 承胤欲殺騰蛟，胤錫劾其罪。

translations.literal: Chengyin wished to kill Tengjiao; Yinxi impeached him for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyin plotted against Tengjiao; Yinxi impeached him.

sentences.zh: 八月，大兵破武岡及寶慶、常德、辰、沅、胤錫走永順土司。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the northern armies took Wugang, Baqing, Changde, Chen, Yuan, and Yinxi fled to the Yongshun tribal domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Qing took Wugang, Baqing, Changde, Chen, and Yuan; Yinxi fled to Yongshun.

sentences.zh: 尋赴貴陽，抵遵義，乞師於皮熊王祥。

translations.literal: Soon he went to Guiyang and Zunyi and begged troops from the tribal king Pi Xiong and Wang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Guiyang and Zunyi and begged troops of Pi Xiong and Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 又入施州，請忠貞營軍。

translations.literal: He again entered Shizhou and asked for the Loyal and Steadfast camp.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Shizhou and sought the Loyal and Steadfast army.

sentences.zh: 會楚宗人朱容藩偽稱監國天下兵馬副元帥，擅居夔州，御史錢邦芑傳檄討之。

translations.literal: Just then the clansman Zhu Rongfan falsely styled himself regent deputy marshal of all armies under Heaven and seized Kui Prefecture; the censor Qian Bangji issued a proclamation to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rongfan falsely claimed regency as deputy marshal and held Kui; Censor Qian Bangji called for his destruction.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，胤錫見容藩，責以大義，曉譬利害，散其黨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year Yinxi saw Rongfan, rebuked him with the great principles, explained advantage and harm, and dispersed his party.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, first month, Yinxi confronted Rongfan, preached duty and interest, and broke up his faction.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金聲桓、李成棟叛我大清，以江西、廣東附永明王。

translations.literal: Before long Jin Shenghuan and Li Chengdong rebelled against the Qing and gave Jiangxi and Guangdong to the Prince of Yongming.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin Shenghuan and Li Chengdong rebelled against the Qing and gave Jiangxi and Guangdong to the Prince.

sentences.zh: 於是馬進忠、王進才、曹誌建、李赤心、高必正等乘間取常德、桃源、澧州、臨武、藍山、道州、靖州、荊門、宜城諸州縣，進忠、赤心，必正皆封公。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ma Jinzhong, Wang Jincai, Cao Zhijian, Li Chixin, Gao Bizheng, and others seized Changde, Taoyuan, Lizhou, Linwu, Lanshan, Daozhou, Jingzhou, Jingmen, Yicheng, and other prefectures and counties; Jinzhong, Chixin, and Bizheng were all enfeoffed as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jinzhong, Wang Jincai, Cao Zhijian, Chixin, and Bizheng then took a string of Hunan cities; Jinzhong, Chixin, and Bizheng became dukes.

sentences.zh: 胤錫與進忠有隙，令赤心、必正爭進忠所取常德，進忠盡焚廬舍而去。

translations.literal: Yinxi was at odds with Jinzhong and ordered Chixin and Bizheng to wrest Changde from him; Jinzhong burned every building as he left.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi quarreled with Jinzhong and sent Chixin and Bizheng against Changde; Jinzhong burned everything as he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 赤心等棄空城引而東，所至守將皆燒營棄城走，湖南已復州縣為一空。

translations.literal: Chixin and the rest abandoned the empty cities and marched east; wherever they went the garrison commanders burned their camps and fled, and the recovered prefectures and counties of Hunan were left void.
translations.idiomatic: Chixin marched east through empty towns as defenders burned camps and fled, leaving recovered Hunan a void.

sentences.zh: 胤錫乃率赤心等入湘潭，與騰蛟會。

translations.literal: Yinxi then led Chixin and the rest into Xiangtan to join Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi led Chixin into Xiangtan to meet Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟令胤錫向江西，而自率進忠等向長沙。

translations.literal: Tengjiao ordered Yinxi toward Jiangxi while he himself led Jinzhong and the rest toward Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao sent Yinxi to Jiangxi and marched on Changsha with Jinzhong.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，兵方逼長沙，騰蛟在湘潭被執，諸軍遂散。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, as the enemy pressed Changsha, Tengjiao was captured at Xiangtan and the armies scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, first month, the enemy closed on Changsha; Tengjiao was taken at Xiangtan and the armies broke up.

sentences.zh: 赤心等走廣西，緣道掠衡、永、郴、桂。

translations.literal: Chixin and the rest fled to Guangxi, plundering Heng, Yong, Chen, and Gui along the way.
translations.idiomatic: Chixin fled to Guangxi, looting Heng, Yong, Chen, and Gui.

sentences.zh: 胤錫與胡一青守衡州，戰敗走桂陽。

translations.literal: Yinxi with Hu Yiqing held Hengzhou, was defeated, and fled to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi and Hu Yiqing held Hengzhou, were beaten, and fled to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 初，赤心等入廣西，龍虎關守將曹誌建惡其淫掠，並惡胤錫。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chixin and the rest entered Guangxi, the Longhu Pass commander Cao Zhijian hated their rapine and also hated Yinxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chixin had first entered Guangxi, Longhu Pass commander Cao Zhijian hated their looting and hated Yinxi as well.

sentences.zh: 胤錫不知也。

translations.literal: Yinxi did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi was unaware.

sentences.zh: 或說誌建，胤錫將召忠貞營圖誌建。

translations.literal: Someone told Zhijian that Yinxi would summon the Zhongzhen Camp to plot against Zhijian.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Zhijian that Yinxi planned to call up the Loyalty Camp to move against him.

sentences.zh: 誌建夜發兵圍胤錫，殺從卒千餘。

translations.literal: Zhijian at night raised troops and besieged Yinxi, killing more than a thousand retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian launched a night attack, encircled Yinxi, and killed over a thousand of his followers.

sentences.zh: 胤錫及子逃入富川瑤峒。

translations.literal: Yinxi and his son fled into the Yao mountain strongholds of Fuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi and his son took refuge in the Yao hill country of Fuchuan.

sentences.zh: 誌建索之急，瑤潛送胤錫於監軍僉事何圖復，間關達梧州。

translations.literal: Zhijian pressed the search urgently; the Yao secretly sent Yinxi to the supervising military assistant He Tufu, who through perilous paths reached Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhijian pressed his hunt relentlessly, the Yao covertly escorted Yinxi to the supervising military assistant He Tufu, who guided him along a perilous route to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會王遣大臣嚴起恒、劉湘客安輯忠貞營。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince dispatched the grand ministers Yan Qiheng and Liu Xiangke to pacify and settle the Zhongzhen Camp.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince sent senior ministers Yan Qiheng and Liu Xiangke to restore order to the Loyalty Camp.

sentences.zh: 至梧而赤心等已走賓、橫二州，乃載胤錫謁王於肇慶。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Wuzhou, Chixin and the rest had already fled to Bin and Heng prefectures; they then brought Yinxi to pay homage to the Prince at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived at Wuzhou, Chixin and his men had already fled to Bin and Heng prefectures; they then conveyed Yinxi to Zhaoqing to audience with the Prince.

sentences.zh: 誌建遷怒圖復，誘殺之，闔門俱盡。

translations.literal: Zhijian redirected his anger onto Tufu, lured and killed him, and wiped out his entire household.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian turned his rage on Tufu, murdered him by deceit, and exterminated his whole family.

sentences.zh: 胤錫至肇慶，時馬吉翔及李元胤、袁彭年等皆專柄，各樹黨。

translations.literal: When Yinxi reached Zhaoqing, at that time Ma Jixiang as well as Li Yuanyin, Yuan Pengnian, and others all monopolized power, each building factions.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Yinxi reached Zhaoqing, Ma Jixiang, Li Yuanyin, Yuan Pengnian, and others had seized power and each forged their own faction.

sentences.zh: 胤錫乃結歡於吉翔，激赤心等東來，與元胤為難。

translations.literal: Yinxi then formed good relations with Jixiang, incited Chixin and the rest to come eastward, and made trouble for Yuanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi courted Jixiang's favor, stirred Chixin and his followers to march east, and set them against Yuanyin.

sentences.zh: 移書瞿式耜，欲間元胤，托言王有密敕，令己與式耜圖元胤，王頗不悅。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Qu Shisi, intending to estrange Yuanyin, claiming falsely that the Prince had a secret order instructing himself and Shisi to plot against Yuanyin; the Prince was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Qu Shisi, seeking to drive a wedge between him and Yuanyin, falsely claiming the Prince had secretly charged the two of them to bring Yuanyin down. The Prince was displeased.

sentences.zh: 元胤黨丁時魁、金堡又論其喪師失地，乃令總統兵馬，移駐梧州。

translations.literal: Yuanyin's partisans Ding Shikui and Jin Bao further accused Yinxi of losing troops and territory; the Prince then ordered him to command all military forces and relocate his headquarters to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyin's allies Ding Shikui and Jin Bao added charges that he had lost armies and territory, and the Prince accordingly appointed him overall commander and ordered him to move his headquarters to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 胤錫以赤心等不足恃，欲遙結孫可望為強援，矯王命封為平遼王。

translations.literal: Yinxi considered Chixin and the rest unreliable, wished to establish distant ties with Sun Kewang as strong support, and forged the Prince's order to ennoble him as Prince of Pingliao.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Chixin and his men unreliable, Yinxi sought a distant alliance with Sun Kewang as a powerful backer and forged a royal patent making Sun Prince of Pingliao.

sentences.zh: 胤錫尋至潯州，自恨發病，十一月卒。

translations.literal: Yinxi soon reached Xunzhou; he fell ill with self-reproach and died in the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxi soon reached Xunzhou, fell ill—perhaps from despair—and died in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 王贈胤錫潯國公，謚文忠。

translations.literal: The Prince posthumously ennobled Yinxi as Duke of Xun and gave him the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince posthumously created Yinxi Duke of Xun and gave him the posthumous title Wenzhong ("Loyal and Upright").

sentences.zh: 嚴起恒

translations.literal: Yan Qiheng
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qiheng

sentences.zh: 嚴起恒，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Yan Qiheng was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qiheng was from Shanyin, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fourth year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 歷廣州知府，遷衡永兵備副使。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Guangzhou, and was transferred to be the vice-commissioner of military preparedness for Heng and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Guangzhou and was later promoted to vice-commissioner for military affairs in Heng and Yong.

sentences.zh: 十六年，張獻忠躪湖南，吏民悉逋竄。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Zhang Xianzhong overran Hunan, and officials and people all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong swept through Hunan, sending officials and commoners fleeing in all directions.

sentences.zh: 起恒獨堅守永州。

translations.literal: Qiheng alone resolutely held Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng alone held firm at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊亦不至。

translations.literal: The bandits also did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels never reached him.

sentences.zh: 唐王時，擢戶部右侍郎，總督湖南錢法。

translations.literal: During the reign of Prince Tang, he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and supervised Hunan's currency policy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Tang he was promoted to vice minister of revenue and put in charge of Hunan's monetary affairs.

sentences.zh: 永明王立，令兼督湖南軍餉。

translations.literal: When the Yongli Prince was enthroned, he was ordered additionally to supervise Hunan's military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongli Prince took the throne, Qiheng was also charged with overseeing Hunan's military rations.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，王駐武岡，拜起恒禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，仍領錢法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, the Prince was stationed at Wugang and appointed Qiheng Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, still retaining charge of the currency policy.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4, with the Prince at Wugang, Qiheng was appointed minister of rites and grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion while retaining his authority over monetary policy.

sentences.zh: 王走靖州，起恒從不及，避難萬村。

translations.literal: The Prince fled to Jingzhou; Qiheng could not follow in time and took refuge at Wancun.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince fled to Jingzhou, Qiheng could not keep up and took shelter at Wancun village.

sentences.zh: 已知王在柳州，閑道往從之。

translations.literal: Once he learned the Prince was at Liuzhou, he went by out-of-the-way paths to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the Prince was at Liuzhou, he made his way there by back roads.

sentences.zh: 從返桂林，復從至柳州、南寧。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince back to Guilin, and again followed to Liuzhou and Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Prince back to Guilin and later to Liuzhou and Nanning.

sentences.zh: 李成棟叛大清，以廣東附於王。

translations.literal: Li Chengdong rebelled against the Great Qing and brought Guangdong over to the Prince's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengdong broke with the Qing and offered Guangdong to the Prince.

sentences.zh: 起恒從王至肇慶，與王化澄、朱天麟同入直。

translations.literal: Qiheng followed the Prince to Zhaoqing and entered daily attendance at court together with Wang Huacheng and Zhu Tianlin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng followed the Prince to Zhaoqing and entered regular attendance at court alongside Wang Huacheng and Zhu Tianlin.

sentences.zh: 無何，化澄、天麟相繼罷。

translations.literal: Before long, Huacheng and Tianlin were dismissed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, both Huacheng and Tianlin were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 黃士俊繼何吾騶為首輔，起恒次之。

translations.literal: Huang Shijun succeeded He Wuzao as chief grand secretary; Qiheng was second.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shijun replaced He Wuzao as chief grand secretary, with Qiheng next in seniority.

sentences.zh: 時朝政決於成棟子元胤，都御史袁彭年，少詹事劉湘客，給事中丁時魁、金堡、蒙正發五人附之，攬權植黨，人目為五虎。

translations.literal: At that time court affairs were decided by Chengdong's son Yuanyin, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Pengnian, Junior Guardian Liu Xiangke, and the supervising secretaries Ding Shikui, Jin Bao, and Meng Zhengfa—the five of them attached to Yuanyin, grasped power and planted factions; people called them the Five Tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Court affairs then rested with Chengdong's son Yuanyin, censor-in-chief Yuan Pengnian, junior guardian Liu Xiangke, and supervising secretaries Ding Shikui, Jin Bao, and Meng Zhengfa, who clustered around Yuanyin, hoarded power, and built cliques. People dubbed them the Five Tigers.

sentences.zh: 起恒居其間，不能有所匡正。

translations.literal: Qiheng stood among them and could not rectify anything.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng stood among them but could do nothing to set matters right.

sentences.zh: 然起恒潔廉，遇事持平，與文安侯馬吉翔、司禮中官龐天壽共患難久，無所忤。

translations.literal: Yet Qiheng was pure and incorrupt, handled affairs even-handedly, and had long shared hardship with the Marquis of Wen'an Ma Jixiang and the director of ceremonies eunuch Pang Tianshou without any friction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qiheng was honest and upright, fair in judgment, and had long weathered hardship alongside Marquis Ma Jixiang of Wen'an and the director of ceremonies eunuch Pang Tianshou without clashing.

sentences.zh: 而五虎憾起恒，競詆為邪黨。

translations.literal: But the Five Tigers resented Qiheng and competed to denounce him as a corrupt faction.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Tigers, however, bore Qiheng a grudge and vied to condemn him as leader of a corrupt clique.

sentences.zh: 王在梧州，尚書吳貞毓等十四人合疏攻五虎，下湘客等獄，欲置之死。

translations.literal: When the Prince was at Wuzhou, Minister Wu Zhengyu and fourteen others jointly memorialized attacking the Five Tigers; Xiangke and the rest were imprisoned, with intent to put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: While the Prince was at Wuzhou, Wu Zhengyu and thirteen other ministers jointly memorialized against the Five Tigers; Liu Xiangke and his allies were thrown into prison, with execution in mind.

sentences.zh: 起恒顧跪王舟力救，貞毓等並惡之，乃請召還化澄，而合攻起恒。

translations.literal: Qiheng turned back, knelt at the Prince's boat, and strove to save them; Zhengyu and the rest hated him as well, then requested the recall of Huacheng and jointly attacked Qiheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng turned back, knelt before the Prince's barge, and pleaded desperately for their lives. Zhengyu and his allies turned on him too, calling for Huacheng's recall and joining forces against Qiheng.

sentences.zh: 給事中雷德復劾其二十餘罪，比之嚴嵩。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Lei Defu impeached him for more than twenty crimes, comparing him to Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Lei Defu charged him with more than twenty offenses, likening him to the corrupt minister Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 王不悅，奪德復官。

translations.literal: The Prince was displeased and stripped Defu of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was displeased and dismissed Defu from office.

sentences.zh: 起恒力求罷，王挽留之不得，放舟竟去。

translations.literal: Qiheng urgently sought dismissal; the Prince could not keep him, and he set sail and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng pressed hard to resign; the Prince could not dissuade him, and he simply boarded his boat and left.

sentences.zh: 會鄖國公高必正入覲王，貞毓欲藉其力以傾起恒，言：「朝事壞於五虎，主之者，起恒也。

translations.literal: When Duke of Yun Gao Bizheng came to audience with the Prince, Zhengyu wished to borrow his force to overthrow Qiheng, saying: "Court affairs were ruined by the Five Tigers, and the one who directed them was Qiheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Gao Bizheng of Yun came to pay homage to the Prince, Zhengyu hoped to use his influence to bring Qiheng down, saying, "Court affairs were ruined by the Five Tigers, and Qiheng was their master.

sentences.zh: 公入見，請除君側奸，數言決矣。

translations.literal: When you enter audience, please eliminate the traitors by the Prince's side; a few words will decide it."
translations.idiomatic: When you see the Prince, ask him to purge the traitors at his side—a few words will settle the matter."

sentences.zh: 」必正許之。

translations.literal: Bizheng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bizheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 有為起恒解者，謂必正曰：「五虎攻嚴公，嚴公反力救五虎。

translations.literal: Someone who spoke for Qiheng said to Bizheng: "The Five Tigers attacked Yan Gong, yet Yan Gong in turn strove to save the Five Tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who spoke up for Qiheng told Bizheng, "The Five Tigers attacked Yan Gong, yet Yan Gong turned around and pleaded to save them.

sentences.zh: 此長者，奈何以為奸？

translations.literal: This is a man of virtue—how can he be deemed a traitor?"
translations.idiomatic: That is the mark of a magnanimous man—how can you call him a traitor?"

sentences.zh: 」必正見王，乃力言起恒虛公可任，請手敕邀與俱還。

translations.literal: When Bizheng saw the Prince, he then strongly argued that Qiheng was an honest and capable man and requested a handwritten edict inviting him to return together.
translations.idiomatic: When Bizheng met the Prince, he spoke forcefully on Qiheng's behalf, praising his integrity and ability, and asked for a personal edict summoning him back.

sentences.zh: 文安之入朝，起恒讓為首輔。

translations.literal: When Wen Zhian entered court, Qiheng yielded the position of chief grand secretary to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Zhian joined the court, Qiheng stepped aside and yielded the chief grand secretaryship to him.

sentences.zh: 桂林破，從王奔南寧。

translations.literal: When Guilin fell, he followed the Prince fleeing to Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: When Guilin fell, he fled with the Prince to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 先是，孫可望據雲南，遣使乞封王。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sun Kewang held Yunnan and sent envoys requesting enfeoffment as king.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sun Kewang had seized Yunnan and sent envoys to request a royal enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 天麟議許之，起恒持不可。

translations.literal: Tianlin advocated granting it; Qiheng held that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin argued it should be granted; Qiheng insisted it must not.

sentences.zh: 後胡執恭矯詔封為秦王，可望知其偽，遣使求真封。

translations.literal: Later Hu Zhigong forged an edict enfeoffing him as King of Qin; Kewang knew it was false and sent envoys requesting a genuine enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hu Zhigong forged an edict making Sun King of Qin. Kewang saw through the fraud and sent envoys demanding a genuine patent.

sentences.zh: 起恒又持不可，可望大怒。

translations.literal: Qiheng again held that it should not be done; Kewang was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng again refused, and Kewang flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 至是，可望知王播遷，遣其將賀九儀、張勝等率勁卒五千，迎王至南寧，直上起恒舟，怒目攘臂，問王封是「秦」非「秦」。

translations.literal: At this time Kewang knew the Prince was displaced, sent his generals He Jiuyi, Zhang Sheng, and others leading five thousand crack troops to welcome the Prince to Nanning, went straight aboard Qiheng's boat, glared and rolled up sleeves, and asked whether the royal enfeoffment was "Qin" or not "Qin."
translations.idiomatic: By then Kewang, learning the Prince was on the run, dispatched his generals He Jiuyi and Zhang Sheng with five thousand elite troops to escort him to Nanning. They boarded Qiheng's boat directly, glaring and brandishing their arms, demanding to know whether the Prince's title would be King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 起恒曰：「君遠迎主上，功甚偉，朝廷自有隆恩。

translations.literal: Qiheng said: "You have come from afar to welcome the sovereign—your merit is very great; the court naturally has lofty favor for you.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng replied, "You have come from afar to welcome the sovereign—a great deed indeed. The court will surely reward you generously.

sentences.zh: 若專問此事，是挾封，非迎主上也。

translations.literal: If you ask only about this matter, that is using enfeoffment as leverage, not welcoming the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: But if you harp on this single matter, you are holding the patent hostage—not welcoming your sovereign at all."

sentences.zh: 」九儀怒，格殺之，投屍於江。

translations.literal: Jiuyi was angered, struck and killed him, and threw the corpse into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyi, enraged, struck him dead and cast his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 遂殺給事中劉堯珍、吳霖、張載述，追殺兵部尚書楊鼎和於昆侖關，皆以阻封議故。

translations.literal: He then killed supervising secretaries Liu Yaozhen, Wu Lin, and Zhang Zaishu, and pursued and killed Minister of War Yang Dinghe at Kunlun Pass—all because they had blocked the enfeoffment proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed supervising secretaries Liu Yaozhen, Wu Lin, and Zhang Zaishu, and pursued and killed Minister of War Yang Dinghe at Kunlun Pass—all for having opposed the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 時順治八年二月也。

translations.literal: It was the second month of the eighth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second month of Shunzhi 8.

sentences.zh: 起恒既死，屍流十餘里，泊沙渚間。

translations.literal: After Qiheng died, the corpse drifted more than ten li and came to rest on a sandbar.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiheng's death his body drifted more than ten li before washing up on a sandbar.

sentences.zh: 虎負之登崖，葬於山麓。

translations.literal: A tiger carried it up the cliff; he was buried at the mountain's foot.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger—so it was said—carried the body ashore; he was buried at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 朱天麟

translations.literal: Zhu Tianlin
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianlin

sentences.zh: 順治四年，永明王居武岡，以禮部侍郎召。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, the Yongli Prince resided at Wugang and summoned Tianlin as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4, with the Yongli Prince at Wugang, Tianlin was summoned as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 天麟疏請王自將，倡率諸鎮，毋坐失事機。

translations.literal: Tianlin memorialized requesting the Prince to lead in person, take the lead among the garrison commanders, and not sit by and lose the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin memorialized urging the Prince to take command in person, rally the regional armies, and not let the moment slip away.

sentences.zh: 辭不至。

translations.literal: He declined and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the summons and did not come.

sentences.zh: 明年，王在南寧，擢禮部尚書，尋拜東閣大學士。

translations.literal: The next year, with the Prince at Nanning, Tianlin was promoted to Minister of Rites and soon appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with the Prince at Nanning, he was promoted to minister of rites and soon appointed grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 天麟請親率士兵略江右，不聽，乃趨謁王。

translations.literal: Tianlin requested to personally lead troops to raid Jiangyou; his request was not granted, and he then hurried to audience with the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin asked permission to lead troops personally into Jiangyou; when refused, he hurried to audience with the Prince.

sentences.zh: 會李成棟反大清，從王至潯州。

translations.literal: At that time Li Chengdong rebelled against the Great Qing, and Tianlin followed the Prince to Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: About then Li Chengdong broke with the Qing, and Tianlin followed the Prince to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 而潯帥陳邦傳請世居廣西如黔國公故事，天麟執不允。

translations.literal: The Xun commander Chen Bangchuan requested hereditary residence in Guangxi after the precedent of the Duke of Qian; Tianlin firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Xun garrison commander Chen Bangchuan petitioned for hereditary residence in Guangxi after the precedent set by the Duke of Qian. Tianlin refused outright.

sentences.zh: 邦傳怒，以慶國公印、尚方劍擲天麟舟中，要必得，仍執不允。

translations.literal: Bangchuan was angered, threw the seal of Duke of Qing and the imperial sword into Tianlin's boat, insisting he must have it, yet Tianlin still firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Bangchuan hurled the seal of the Duke of Qing and an imperial sword into Tianlin's boat, demanding an answer—but Tianlin still refused.

sentences.zh: 已而成棟奉王駐肇慶，天麟謂機可乘，復勸王亟頒親征詔，規取中原。

translations.literal: Before long Chengdong escorted the Prince to reside at Zhaoqing; Tianlin considered the opportunity could be seized and again urged the Prince promptly to issue a personal-campaign edict, planning to recover the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chengdong brought the Prince to Zhaoqing. Tianlin judged the moment ripe and again urged him to proclaim a personal campaign and plan the reconquest of the north.

sentences.zh: 王優詔答之。

translations.literal: The Prince replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朝臣各樹黨。

translations.literal: At that time court ministers each built factions.
translations.idiomatic: By then every minister at court had carved out a faction.

sentences.zh: 從成棟至者，曹曄、耿獻忠、洪天擢、潘曾緯、毛毓祥、李綺，自誇反正功，氣淩朝士。

translations.literal: Those who came with Chengdong—Cao Ye, Geng Xianzhong, Hong Tianzhuo, Pan Cengwei, Mao Yuxiang, Li Qi—boasted of their achievement in returning to allegiance and lorded it over the court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had come with Chengdong—Cao Ye, Geng Xianzhong, Hong Tianzhuo, Pan Cengwei, Mao Yuxiang, and Li Qi—trumpeted their turncoat merit and looked down on the court.

sentences.zh: 從廣西扈行至者，天麟及嚴起恒、王化澄、晏清、吳貞毓、吳其雷、洪士彭、雷德復、尹三聘、許兆進、張孝起，自恃舊臣，詆曹、耿等嘗事異姓。

translations.literal: Those who had escorted the Prince from Guangxi—Tianlin as well as Yan Qiheng, Wang Huacheng, Yan Qing, Wu Zhengyu, Wu Qilei, Hong Shipeng, Lei Defu, Yin Sanpin, Xu Zhaojin, and Zhang Xiaoqi—relied on being old ministers and denounced Cao, Geng, and the rest for once serving alien surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had escorted the Prince from Guangxi—Tianlin, Yan Qiheng, Wang Huacheng, Yan Qing, Wu Zhengyu, Wu Qilei, Hong Shipeng, Lei Defu, Yin Sanpin, Xu Zhaojin, and Zhang Xiaoqi—claimed the status of loyal old hands and reviled Cao, Geng, and their ilk for having once served the foreign dynasty.

sentences.zh: 久之復分吳、楚兩黨。

translations.literal: Before long they again divided into Wu and Chu factions.
translations.idiomatic: In time the court split again into Wu and Chu factions.

sentences.zh: 主吳者，天麟、孝起、貞毓、李用楫、堵胤錫、王化澄、萬翺、程源、郭之奇，皆內結馬吉翔，外結陳邦傳。

translations.literal: Leaders of the Wu faction were Tianlin, Xiaoqi, Zhengyu, Li Yongji, Du Yinxi, Wang Huacheng, Wan Hao, Cheng Yuan, and Guo Zhiqi—all inwardly allied with Ma Jixiang and outwardly allied with Chen Bangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu faction was led by Tianlin, Xiaoqi, Zhengyu, Li Yongji, Du Yinxi, Wang Huacheng, Wan Hao, Cheng Yuan, and Guo Zhiqi, who aligned with Ma Jixiang within the court and Chen Bangchuan without.

sentences.zh: 主楚者，袁彭年、丁時魁、蒙正發、劉湘客、金堡，皆外結瞿式耜，內結李元胤。

translations.literal: Leaders of the Chu faction were Yuan Pengnian, Ding Shikui, Meng Zhengfa, Liu Xiangke, and Jin Bao—all outwardly allied with Qu Shisi and inwardly allied with Li Yuanyin.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu faction was led by Yuan Pengnian, Ding Shikui, Meng Zhengfa, Liu Xiangke, and Jin Bao, allied outwardly with Qu Shisi and inwardly with Li Yuanyin.

sentences.zh: 元胤者，惠國公成棟子，為錦衣指揮使，進封南陽伯，握大權。

translations.literal: Yuanyin was the son of Duke of Huiguo Chengdong, served as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was advanced to Earl of Nanyang, and held great power.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyin was the son of Duke Chengdong of Huiguo, a commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard elevated to Earl of Nanyang, and he wielded enormous power.

sentences.zh: 彭年等倚為心腹，勢張甚。

translations.literal: Pengnian and the rest relied on him as their intimate; their power expanded greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian and his allies leaned on him as their patron, and their power swelled accordingly.

sentences.zh: 彭年嘗論事王前，語不遜。

translations.literal: Pengnian once discussed affairs before the Prince; his words were disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Once, debating policy before the Prince, Pengnian spoke with shocking insolence.

sentences.zh: 王責以君臣之義，彭年勃然曰：「儻向者惠國以五千鐵騎，鼓行而西，君臣義安在？

translations.literal: The Prince rebuked him on the basis of the lord-and-subject relationship; Pengnian suddenly said: "Had Duke of Huiguo not led five thousand iron cavalry westward with drums beating, where would the lord-and-subject relationship be?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince rebuked him for forgetting the bond between sovereign and subject. Pengnian flushed with anger and said, "If Duke Huiguo had not marched five thousand armored horsemen west with drums beating, what bond between sovereign and subject would there be?"

sentences.zh: 」王變色，大惡之。

translations.literal: The Prince changed color and greatly hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince turned pale and took a deep dislike to him.

sentences.zh: 彭年等謀攻去吉翔、邦傳，權可獨擅也。

translations.literal: Pengnian and the rest plotted to attack and remove Jixiang and Bangchuan so that power could be monopolized alone.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian and his allies plotted to drive out Jixiang and Bangchuan so they could keep power for themselves.

sentences.zh: 而堡居言路，有鋒氣，乃疏陳八事，劾慶國公邦傳十可斬，文安侯吉翔，司禮中官龐天壽，大學士起恒、化澄與焉。

translations.literal: Jin Bao occupied the remonstrance path and had a sharp edge; he then memorialized setting forth eight matters, impeaching Duke of Qing Bangchuan for ten capital crimes, and including Marquis of Wen'an Jixiang, the director of ceremonies eunuch Pang Tianshou, and grand secretaries Qiheng and Huacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Bao held the censor's post and struck boldly: he memorialized on eight points, called for the execution of Duke Bangchuan of Qing on ten capital counts, and named Marquis Jixiang of Wen'an, the director of ceremonies eunuch Pang Tianshou, and grand secretaries Qiheng and Huacheng.

sentences.zh: 起恒、化澄乞去，天麟奏留之。

translations.literal: Qiheng and Huacheng requested resignation; Tianlin memorialized to retain them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng and Huacheng asked to resign; Tianlin memorialized that they be kept in place.

sentences.zh: 堡與給事中時魁等復相繼劾起恒、吉翔、天壽無已。

translations.literal: Jin Bao and supervising secretaries Shikui and the rest again in succession impeached Qiheng, Jixiang, and Tianshou without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Bao and supervising secretaries including Shikui kept filing impeachments against Qiheng, Jixiang, and Tianshou without letup.

sentences.zh: 太后召天麟面諭，武岡危難，賴吉翔左右，令擬諭嚴責堡等。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned Tianlin and orally instructed him: at Wugang's peril they had relied on Jixiang at the Prince's side; she ordered him to draft an edict severely reproaching Bao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager summoned Tianlin and told him that in the crisis at Wugang they had depended on Jixiang at the Prince's side; she ordered him to draft a stern edict rebuking Bao and his allies.

sentences.zh: 天麟為兩解，卒未嘗罪言者，而彭年輩怒不止。

translations.literal: Tianlin made explanations for both sides; in the end he never punished the memorialists, yet Pengnian and the rest did not cease their anger.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin tried to mollify both sides and ultimately never punished the memorialists—but Pengnian and his faction remained furious.

sentences.zh: 王知群臣水火甚，令盟於太廟，然黨益固不能解。

translations.literal: The Prince knew the ministers were bitter as fire and water; he ordered them to swear an oath at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, yet the factions grew firmer and could not be dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how irreconcilably the ministers opposed one another, the Prince ordered them to swear an oath at the Imperial Ancestral Temple—but the factions only hardened and could not be bridged.

sentences.zh: 明年春，邦傳訐堡官臨清嘗降流賊，受其職，且請堡為己監軍。

translations.literal: The next spring, Bangchuan denounced Bao, saying that when stationed at Linqing he had once surrendered to bandits and accepted their commission, and further requested Bao as his supervising commander.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Bangchuan accused Bao of having surrendered to bandits while stationed at Linqing and accepting their commission; he also petitioned to have Bao appointed as his supervising commander.

sentences.zh: 天麟因擬諭譏堡，堡大憤。

translations.literal: Tianlin accordingly drafted an edict ridiculing Bao; Bao was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin drafted an edict mocking Bao in response, and Bao was furious.

sentences.zh: 時魁乃鼓言官十六人詣閣詆天麟，至登殿陛大嘩，棄官擲印而出。

translations.literal: Shikui then stirred sixteen censorial officials to go to the Grand Secretariat and denounce Tianlin, reaching the point of mounting the palace steps with loud clamor, abandoning office and throwing down seals as they left.
translations.idiomatic: Shikui rallied sixteen remonstrating officials to storm the Grand Secretariat and denounce Tianlin; they mounted the palace steps shouting, then cast aside their seals and walked out.

sentences.zh: 王方坐後殿，與侍臣論事，大驚，兩手交戰，茶傾於衣，急取還天麟所擬而罷。

translations.literal: The Prince was just then seated in the rear hall discussing affairs with attendant ministers; greatly alarmed, his two hands trembled, tea spilled on his robes; he urgently had Tianlin's draft retrieved and abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was conferring with his attendants in the rear hall when the uproar broke out. He was badly shaken—his hands trembled and tea spilled on his robe—and he quickly had Tianlin's draft withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 天麟遂辭位，王慰留再三，不可。

translations.literal: Tianlin then resigned his position; the Prince comforted him and repeatedly urged him to stay, but he would not.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin resigned. The Prince entreated him repeatedly to stay, but he would not.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，叩頭泣。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he kowtowed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he kowtowed and wept.

sentences.zh: 王亦泣曰：「卿去，余益孤矣。」

translations.literal: The Prince also wept and said: "With you gone, I am all the more alone."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince wept as well and said, "With you gone, I am more alone than ever."

sentences.zh: 初，時魁等謂所擬出起恒意，欲入署毆之。

translations.literal: At first Shikui and the rest believed the draft had come from Qiheng's intentions and wished to enter the office and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shikui and his allies thought Qiheng had authored the draft and planned to enter his office and beat him.

sentences.zh: 是日，起恒不入，而天麟獨自承。

translations.literal: That day Qiheng did not enter; Tianlin alone took responsibility upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: That day Qiheng stayed away, and Tianlin shouldered the blame alone.

sentences.zh: 遂移怒天麟，逐之去，天麟移居慶遠。

translations.literal: They then redirected their anger onto Tianlin, drove him out, and Tianlin moved to reside at Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned their wrath on Tianlin and drove him out; he relocated to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 化澄貪鄙無物望，亦為時魁等所攻，碎冠服辭去。

translations.literal: Huacheng was greedy and base, without public esteem; he too was attacked by Shikui and the rest, shattered his cap and robes, and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng was grasping and contemptible, held in no public regard; Shikui and his allies turned on him too, and he smashed his official cap and robes and quit office.

sentences.zh: 王乃召何吾騶、黃士俊入輔。

translations.literal: The Prince then summoned He Wuzhou and Huang Shijun to enter the Grand Secretariat as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince then called He Wuzhou and Huang Shijun into the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吾騶亦為堡等排去，獨士俊、起恒在，乃復召天麟，天麟不至。

translations.literal: Before long, Wuzhou was also driven out by Bao and the rest; only Shijun and Qiheng remained. The Prince then again summoned Tianlin, but Tianlin did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Bao and his faction drove Wuzhou out as well, leaving only Shijun and Qiheng in office. The Prince summoned Tianlin again, but Tianlin refused to come.

sentences.zh: 堡等既連逐三相，益橫，每闌入閣中，授閣臣以意指。

translations.literal: Bao and the rest, having in succession driven out three Grand Secretaries, grew still more overbearing; they would force their way into the Grand Secretariat and dictate their intentions to the Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Having already hounded three Grand Secretaries from office, Bao and his allies grew bolder still. They barged into the Grand Secretariat and told the ministers what to write.

sentences.zh: 王不得已，建文華殿於正殿旁，令閣臣侍坐擬旨以避之。

translations.literal: The Prince had no choice but to build a Wenhua Hall beside the main hall and have the Grand Secretaries sit there drafting edicts to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince had no choice but to build a Wenhua Hall beside the throne hall and have the Grand Secretaries sit there drafting edicts—simply to keep Bao's crowd at bay.

sentences.zh: 堡又連劾堵胤錫及侍郎萬翺、程源、郭之奇，尚書吳貞毓。

translations.literal: Bao again filed successive impeachments against Du Yinxi and Vice Ministers Wan Ao, Cheng Yuan, and Guo Zhiqi, and Minister Wu Zhenyu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao next launched a barrage of impeachments against Du Yinxi, Vice Ministers Wan Ao, Cheng Yuan, and Guo Zhiqi, and Minister Wu Zhenyu.

sentences.zh: 貞毓等欲排去之，畏元胤為援，不敢發。

translations.literal: Zhenyu and the rest wished to drive Bao out but feared Yuanyin as his backing and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu and his allies wanted Bao removed but feared Yuanyin's protection and held back.

sentences.zh: 七年春，王赴梧州，元胤留肇慶，陳邦傳適遣兵入衛。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, the Prince went to Wuzhou; Yuanyin remained at Zhaoqing; Chen Bangchuan happened to dispatch troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year the Prince traveled to Wuzhou while Yuanyin stayed at Zhaoqing; Chen Bangchuan happened to send troops to guard the court.

sentences.zh: 貞毓、之奇、翺、源乃合諸給事御史劾彭年、湘客、時魁、堡、正發把持朝政，罔上行私罪。

translations.literal: Zhenyu, Zhiqi, Ao, and Yuan then joined the supervising secretaries and censors in impeaching Pengnian, Xiangke, Shikui, Bao, and Zhengfa for monopolizing court governance and deceiving the sovereign for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu, Zhiqi, Ao, and Yuan rallied the supervising secretaries and censors to impeach Pengnian, Xiangke, Shikui, Bao, and Zhengfa for seizing control of the court and deceiving the throne for private gain.

sentences.zh: 王謂彭年反正有功，免議，下堡等獄。

translations.literal: The Prince said Pengnian had merit in returning to allegiance and exempted him from the inquiry; he imprisoned Bao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince ruled that Pengnian deserved credit for returning to allegiance and spared him further inquiry, but sent Bao and his allies to prison.

sentences.zh: 堡又以語觸忌，與時魁並謫戍。

translations.literal: Bao again gave offense with his words; he and Shikui were both banished to border garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Bao again spoke out of turn and gave offense; he and Shikui were both banished to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 湘客、正發贖配追臟。

translations.literal: Xiangke and Zhengfa were sentenced to penal servitude by ransom and ordered to pay restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangke and Zhengfa were sentenced to penal servitude and ordered to pay restitution.

sentences.zh: 王乃再召天麟，天麟疏言：「年來百爾構爭，盡壞實事。

translations.literal: The Prince again summoned Tianlin. Tianlin memorialized: "For years factional strife has ruined all practical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince summoned Tianlin once more. Tianlin memorialized: "For years your ministers have torn one another apart, and every practical task has been ruined.

sentences.zh: 昔宋高宗航海，猶有退步。

translations.literal: In the past, when Emperor Gaozong of Song took to the sea, he still had somewhere to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong of Song put to sea, he still had somewhere to fall back.

sentences.zh: 今則何地可退？

translations.literal: But where can we retreat today?
translations.idiomatic: Where can we retreat now?

sentences.zh: 當奮然自將，文武諸臣盡擐甲胄。

translations.literal: We should rouse ourselves and personally lead the armies; civil and military ministers alike should don armor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should rouse yourself and take the field in person; every civil and military minister should buckle on armor.

sentences.zh: 臣亦抽峒丁，擇土豪，募水手，經略嶺北、湖南，為六軍倡。

translations.literal: I too will levy hill-tribesmen, select local strongmen, recruit sailors, and pacify the lands north of the Ling and in Hunan, to lead the six armies forward.
translations.idiomatic: I will levy hill tribesmen, choose local strongmen, recruit sailors, and pacify the country north of the Ling and in Hunan—to lead the six armies forward.

sentences.zh: 若徒責票擬，以為主持政本，今政本安在乎？」

translations.literal: If you merely hold me to drafting memorial responses and call that governing the state, where does the substance of governance lie now?"
translations.idiomatic: If you only hold me to drafting edicts and call that holding the reins of government, where is the substance of government today?"

sentences.zh: 時大兵益逼，孫可望請王赴雲南。

translations.literal: At that time the Qing armies pressed closer; Sun Kewang asked the Prince to come to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing armies were pressing closer, and Sun Kewang invited the Prince to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 初，起恒持可望封，天麟及化澄獨謂宜許。

translations.literal: At first Qiheng opposed enfeoffing Kewang; Tianlin and Huacheng alone argued it should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qiheng opposed granting Kewang a royal title; only Tianlin and Huacheng argued it should be allowed.

sentences.zh: 及可望使至，天麟力請從之。

translations.literal: When Kewang's envoy arrived, Tianlin strongly urged compliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang's envoy arrived, Tianlin pressed hard for the court to accept.

sentences.zh: 請臣以起恒被殺故，皆不可。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers, citing Qiheng's murder, all refused.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers, citing Qiheng's murder, all refused.

sentences.zh: 天麟乃奉命經略左、右兩江土司，以為勤王之助。

translations.literal: Tianlin then accepted orders to pacify the tribal chiefs of the Left and Right River regions, to aid the effort to rescue the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin then took orders to pacify the tribal chiefs of the Left and Right Rivers, to support the effort to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 兵未集，大兵逼南寧，王倉皇出走，天麟扶病從之。

translations.literal: Before the troops had assembled, the Qing armies pressed Nanning; the Prince fled in panic and Tianlin, though ill, followed.
translations.idiomatic: Before his troops had gathered, the Qing armies closed on Nanning. The Prince fled in panic, and Tianlin, though sick, went with him.

sentences.zh: 明年四月抵廣南，王已先駐安龍。

translations.literal: The following year, in the fourth month, he reached Guangnan; the Prince had already established himself at Anlong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the fourth month, he reached Guangnan; the Prince had already taken up residence at Anlong.

sentences.zh: 天麟病劇，不能入覲，卒於西阪村。

translations.literal: Tianlin's illness grew severe; he could not attend audience and died at Xiban Village.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin's illness worsened until he could no longer attend audience; he died at Xiban Village.

sentences.zh: 張孝起

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoqi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoqi

sentences.zh: 張孝起，吳江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoqi was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoqi was a native of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，授廉州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 大兵至，逼海濱，舉兵謀恢復。

translations.literal: When the Qing armies arrived, pressing the seacoast, he raised troops to recover the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing armies reached the coast, he raised troops to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 戰敗被獲，妻妾俱投海死。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle and captured, his wives and concubines all drowned themselves in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated and captured, he watched his wives and concubines throw themselves into the sea.

sentences.zh: 孝起羈軍中，會李成棟叛大清，孝起乃脫去。

translations.literal: Xiaoqi was held captive in the army; when Li Chengdong rebelled against the Qing, Xiaoqi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoqi was held in the enemy camp until Li Chengdong rebelled against the Qing; then he broke free.

sentences.zh: 永明王以為吏科給事中。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui appointed him supervising secretary of the Office of Personnel Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui made him supervising secretary of the Office of Personnel Affairs.

sentences.zh: 清真介直，不與流俗伍。

translations.literal: Upright, pure, and stern, he would not consort with the vulgar crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and incorruptible, he kept his distance from the vulgar world.

sentences.zh: 王至梧州。

translations.literal: The Prince reached Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince arrived at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉湘客、丁時魁、金堡、蒙正發以失李元胤援，並辭職。

translations.literal: Liu Xiangke, Ding Shikui, Jin Bao, and Meng Zhengfa, having lost Li Yuanyin's backing, all resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiangke, Ding Shikui, Jin Bao, and Meng Zhengfa, having lost Li Yuanyin's support, all resigned.

sentences.zh: 王報許，以孝起代時魁，掌吏科印。

translations.literal: The Prince assented and had Xiaoqi replace Shikui in charge of the Office of Personnel Affairs seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince agreed and put Xiaoqi in Shikui's place, entrusting him with the Office of Personnel Affairs seal.

sentences.zh: 俄與廷臣共排去湘客等，遂為其黨所疾。

translations.literal: Soon he joined the court ministers in driving out Xiangke and the rest, and thus became hated by their faction.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he joined the court ministers in driving out Xiangke and his allies, and their faction came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 高必正，湘客鄉人也，尤疾之，怒罵於朝，王為解乃已。

translations.literal: Gao Bizheng, a fellow townsman of Xiangke, hated him especially; he raged and cursed him at court until the Prince mediated and it ended.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bizheng, Xiangke's fellow townsman, hated him above all; he raged and cursed him in open court until the Prince intervened.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢孝起右僉都御史，巡撫高、雷、廉、瓊四府。

translations.literal: After some time Xiaoqi was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made military governor of the four prefectures of Gaozhou, Leizhou, Lianzhou, and Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In time Xiaoqi was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made military governor of Gaozhou, Leizhou, Lianzhou, and Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 城破，走避龍門島。

translations.literal: When the city fell he fled to Longmen Island.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he fled to Longmen Island.

sentences.zh: 島破，被執，不食七日死。

translations.literal: When the island fell he was captured and starved himself for seven days until he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the island fell he was taken prisoner and refused food for seven days until he died.

sentences.zh: 楊畏知

translations.literal: Yang Weizhi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhi

sentences.zh: 楊畏知，寶雞人。

translations.literal: Yang Weizhi was a native of Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhi was a native of Baoji.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，歷官雲南副使，分巡金滄。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he served as Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, with circuit responsibility over Jin and Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he rose to Vice Commissioner of Yunnan with circuit responsibility over Jin and Cang.

sentences.zh: 乙酉秋，武定土官吾必奎反，連陷祿豐、廣通諸縣及楚雄府。

translations.literal: In the autumn of yiyou, the native official of Wuding, Wu Bikui, rebelled and in succession captured the counties of Lufeng and Guangtong and Chuxiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of yiyou the native official of Wuding, Wu Bikui, rebelled and in quick succession overran Lufeng, Guangtong, and Chuxiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 畏知督兵復楚雄，駐其地。

translations.literal: Weizhi directed troops to recover Chuxiong and garrisoned the place.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi led troops to retake Chuxiong and held the city.

sentences.zh: 必奎伏誅，而阿迷土官沙定洲繼亂，據雲南，黔國公沐天波走楚雄。

translations.literal: Bikui was executed, but the native official of Ami, Sha Dingzhou, continued the rebellion, seized Yunnan, and Duke Mu Tianbo fled to Chuxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Bikui was put to death, but Sha Dingzhou, the native official of Ami, took up the revolt, seized Yunnan, and Duke Mu Tianbo fled to Chuxiong.

sentences.zh: 巡撫吳兆元不能制，許為奏請鎮雲南。

translations.literal: The military governor Wu Zhaoyuan could not suppress him and promised to memorialize requesting authority to pacify Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Wu Zhaoyuan could not contain him and promised to memorialize the throne for authority to pacify Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 定洲遂西追天波，畏知說天波走永昌，而己以楚雄當定洲。

translations.literal: Dingzhou then pursued Tianbo westward; Weizhi persuaded Tianbo to flee to Yongchang while he himself held Chuxiong against Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou pressed west after Tianbo; Weizhi urged Tianbo to flee to Yongchang while he himself stood at Chuxiong to block Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 定洲至，畏知復紿之曰：「若所急者，黔國爾，今已西。

translations.literal: When Dingzhou arrived, Weizhi again deceived him, saying: "What you urgently want is the Duke of Qian—he has already gone west.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingzhou arrived, Weizhi deceived him again: "What you want is the Duke of Qian, and he has already gone west.

sentences.zh: 待爾定永昌還，朝命當已下，予出城以禮見。

translations.literal: Wait until you settle Yongchang and return; the court order should have arrived by then, and I will leave the city to receive you with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until you have settled Yongchang and returned; by then the court's orders should have come down, and I will leave the city to receive you with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今順逆未分，不能為不義屈也。

translations.literal: As loyalty and rebellion are not yet settled, I cannot bow to injustice."
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and rebellion are not yet decided; I cannot submit to what is unjust."

sentences.zh: 」定洲恐失天波，與盟而去。

translations.literal: Dingzhou, fearing he would lose Tianbo, made an alliance with him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou, afraid of losing Tianbo, made a pact with Weizhi and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 分兵陷大理、蒙化。

translations.literal: He divided his forces and captured Dali and Monhua.
translations.idiomatic: He split his forces and took Dali and Monhua.

sentences.zh: 畏知乘間清野繕堞，征鄰境援兵，姚安、景東俱響應。

translations.literal: Weizhi seized the interval to clear the countryside and repair the walls, raising relief troops from neighboring districts; Yao'an and Jingdong both responded.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi used the lull to clear the countryside, repair the walls, and summon aid from neighboring districts; Yao'an and Jingdong both answered his call.

sentences.zh: 定洲聞，不敢至永昌，還攻楚雄，不能下。

translations.literal: When Dingzhou heard this, he dared not advance to Yongchang; he returned to attack Chuxiong but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Dingzhou dared not push on to Yongchang; he turned back to besiege Chuxiong but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 畏知伺賊懈，輒出擊，殺傷多。

translations.literal: Weizhi watched for moments when the rebels slackened and sallied forth repeatedly, inflicting many casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi watched for slack moments in the rebel lines and sallied out again and again, inflicting heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 乃引去，還攻石屏、寧州、習峨，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Then he withdrew and turned to attack Shiping, Ningzhou, and Xi'e—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew and turned on Shiping, Ningzhou, and Xi'e, capturing them all.

sentences.zh: 復西攻楚雄，迄不能下。

translations.literal: He again attacked Chuxiong from the west but still could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Chuxiong from the west once more but still could not break the city.

sentences.zh: 明年，孫可望等入雲南，定洲還救，大敗，遁歸阿迷，可望等遂據會城。

translations.literal: The next year Sun Kewang and the others entered Yunnan; Dingzhou returned to relieve the siege, suffered a great defeat, fled back to Ami, and Kewang and his allies then held the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Sun Kewang and his forces entered Yunnan. Dingzhou rushed back to relieve the siege, was routed, and fled to Ami; Kewang and his allies then held the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 初，唐王聞畏知抗賊，進授右僉都御史，巡撫雲南，以巡撫吳兆元為總督。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Tang heard that Weizhi was resisting the rebels, he promoted him to Right Censor-in-Chief and made him military governor of Yunnan, with Wu Zhaoyuan as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Prince of Tang learned that Weizhi was holding out against the rebels, he promoted him to Right Censor-in-Chief and military governor of Yunnan, with Wu Zhaoyuan as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 及可望等至，以畏知同鄉，甚重之。

translations.literal: When Kewang and the others arrived, finding Weizhi was a fellow townsman, they greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang arrived, he learned Weizhi was a fellow townsman and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 尋與劉文秀西略，畏知拒戰敗，投水不死，踞而罵。

translations.literal: Soon, campaigning west with Liu Wenxiu, Weizhi was defeated in battle; he threw himself into the water but did not die, and squatted there cursing them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, campaigning west with Liu Wenxiu, Weizhi was beaten in battle. He threw himself into the water but did not drown; he squatted on the bank and cursed them.

sentences.zh: 可望下馬慰之曰：「聞公名久。

translations.literal: Kewang dismounted to comfort him, saying: "I have long heard your name.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang dismounted to comfort him: "I have long known your name.

sentences.zh: 吾為討賊來，公能共事，相與匡扶明室，非有他也。

translations.literal: I have come to suppress bandits. If you can work with me in restoring the Ming house, I want nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: I came to suppress the bandits. If you will work with me to restore the Ming house, I ask for nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」畏知瞪目視之曰：「紿我爾。

translations.literal: Weizhi stared wide-eyed and said: "You are deceiving me."
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi glared at him and said: "You are lying to me."

sentences.zh: 」可望曰：「不信，當折矢誓。

translations.literal: Kewang said: "If you don't believe me, I shall break an arrow in oath."
translations.idiomatic: Kewang said: "If you do not believe me, I will break an arrow and swear."

sentences.zh: 」畏知曰：「果爾，當從我三事：一不得仍用偽西年號，二不得殺人，三不得焚廬舍，淫婦女。

translations.literal: Weizhi said: "If it is truly so, then you must agree to three things: first, you must not continue using the false Western year title; second, you must not kill people; third, you must not burn dwellings or violate women."
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi said: "If you mean it, then agree to three things: first, do not keep using the false Western reign title; second, do not kill; third, do not burn homes or abuse women."

sentences.zh: 」可望皆許諾。

translations.literal: Kewang promised them all.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang agreed to all three.

sentences.zh: 乃與至楚雄，略定大理諸郡，使文秀至永昌迎天波歸。

translations.literal: He then went with him to Chuxiong, subdued the prefectures around Dali, and sent Wenxiu to Yongchang to escort Tianbo home.
translations.idiomatic: He then went with Weizhi to Chuxiong, pacified the prefectures around Dali, and sent Wenxiu to Yongchang to bring Tianbo home.

sentences.zh: 迤西八府免屠戮，畏知力也。

translations.literal: That the eight prefectures of far western Yunnan were spared slaughter was Weizhi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: That the eight prefectures of far western Yunnan were spared massacre was Weizhi's work.

sentences.zh: 時永明王已稱號於肇慶，而詔令不至。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Gui had already proclaimed his reign at Zhaoqing, but his edicts had not reached them.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Prince of Gui had already proclaimed his reign at Zhaoqing, but his edicts had not yet reached Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 前御史臨安任僎議尊可望為國主，以幹支紀年，鑄興朝通寶錢。

translations.literal: The former censor of Lin'an, Ren Fu, proposed to honor Kewang as sovereign, use the sexagenary cycle for the reign, and cast Xingchao Tongbao coinage.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu, former censor of Lin'an, proposed honoring Kewang as sovereign, dating the reign by the sexagenary cycle, and casting Xingchao Tongbao coinage.

sentences.zh: 畏知憤甚，有所忤，輒抵掌謾罵。

translations.literal: Weizhi was furious; whenever something offended him he would slap his palms and hurl abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi was incensed; at the slightest provocation he would slap his hands together and hurl abuse.

sentences.zh: 可望數欲殺之，李定國、劉文秀為保護得免。

translations.literal: Kewang repeatedly wanted to kill him; Li Dingguo and Liu Wenxiu protected him and he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang tried more than once to kill him, but Li Dingguo and Liu Wenxiu shielded him and he survived.

sentences.zh: 可望與劉、李同輩，一旦自尊，兩人不為下。

translations.literal: Kewang had been peers with Liu and Li; now that he suddenly elevated himself, the two would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang had once been Liu's and Li's equal; now that he raised himself above them, neither would bow.

sentences.zh: 聞肇慶有君，李錦、李成棟等並加封爵，念得朝命，加王封，庶可相制，乃議遣使奉表。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhaoqing had a sovereign and that Li Jin, Li Chengdong, and others had all received ennoblement, they thought that if they obtained a court patent and a princely title for their leader, they might check one another—and so they discussed sending envoys with a memorial of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhaoqing had a sovereign and that Li Jin, Li Chengdong, and others had all received titles, they reasoned that a court patent and a royal enfeoffment for their leader might keep one another in check, and so they discussed sending envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 畏知亦素以尊主為言。

translations.literal: Weizhi too had always spoken of honoring the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi, for his part, had always argued for honoring the throne.

sentences.zh: 歲已醜，遣畏知及永昌故兵部郎中龔彜赴肇慶進可望表，請王封，為金堡等所持。

translations.literal: In the jichou year they sent Weizhi and the former Bureau Director of War at Yongchang, Gong Yi, to Zhaoqing to present Kewang's memorial requesting a royal enfeoffment; they were detained by Jin Bao and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the jichou year they sent Weizhi and Gong Yi, former Bureau Director of War at Yongchang, to Zhaoqing with Kewang's memorial requesting a royal title; Jin Bao and his allies detained them.

sentences.zh: 畏知乃曰：「可望欲權出劉、李上爾。

translations.literal: Weizhi then said: "Kewang merely wants authority above Liu and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi then said: "Kewang only wants rank above Liu and Li.

sentences.zh: 今晉之上公，而卑劉、李侯爵可也。

translations.literal: If we now promote him to Grand Duke and demote Liu and Li to marquisates, that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Promote him to Grand Duke and leave Liu and Li as marquises—that should be enough."

sentences.zh: 」乃議封可望景國公，賜名朝宗；

translations.literal: They then agreed to enfeoff Kewang as Duke of Jing and grant him the name Chaozong;
translations.idiomatic: They then resolved to enfeoff Kewang as Duke of Jing and grant him the name Chaozong;

sentences.zh: 定國、文秀皆列侯。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxiu were both made marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu were both given marquisates.

sentences.zh: 遣大理卿趙昱為使，加畏知兵部尚書，彜兵部侍郎，同行。

translations.literal: They dispatched Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zhao Yu as envoy, promoted Weizhi to Minister of War and Yi to Vice Minister of War, and sent them together.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Zhao Yu, Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, as envoy, promoted Weizhi to Minister of War and Yi to Vice Minister of War, and dispatched them together.

sentences.zh: 時堵胤錫曾賜空敕，得便宜行事。

translations.literal: At that time Du Yinxi had been granted a blank patent empowering discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yinxi had recently been given a blank patent authorizing discretionary action.

sentences.zh: 昱乃就與謀，矯命改封可望平遼王，易敕書以往。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu then consulted with him and forged an order changing Kewang's enfeoffment to Prince of Pingliao, swapping the patent and proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu then conspired with him, forged an order changing Kewang's title to Prince of Pingliao, replaced the patent, and set out.

sentences.zh: 武康伯胡執恭者，慶國公陳邦傳中軍也，守泗城。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Hu Zhigong of Wukang was middle army commander under Duke Chen Bangchuan and guarded Sicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhigong, Military Commissioner of Wukang, was middle-army commander under Duke Chen Bangchuan and held Sicheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州與雲南接，欲自結可望，言於邦傳，先矯命封可望秦王，曰：「藉其力可制李赤心也。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered Yunnan; wishing to ally himself with Kewang, he spoke to Bangchuan and first forged an order enfeoffing Kewang as King of Qin, saying: "With his strength we can control Li Chixin."
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng bordered Yunnan; hoping to win Kewang's favor, he spoke to Bangchuan and first forged an order enfeoffing Kewang as King of Qin, saying: "With his strength we can control Li Chixin."

sentences.zh: 」邦傳乃鑄金章曰：「秦王之寶」，填所給空敕，令執恭賫行。

translations.literal: Bangchuan then cast a golden seal reading "Seal of the King of Qin," filled in the blank patent he had been given, and ordered Zhigong to carry them.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchuan cast a golden seal reading "Seal of the King of Qin," filled in the blank patent he had received, and ordered Zhigong to deliver them.

sentences.zh: 可望大喜，郊迎。

translations.literal: Kewang was overjoyed and went out to the suburbs to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang was delighted and went out to the suburbs to welcome the envoy.

sentences.zh: 亡何，畏知等至。

translations.literal: Before long Weizhi and the others arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Weizhi and his party arrived.

sentences.zh: 可望駭不受，曰：「我已封秦王矣。

translations.literal: Kewang, startled, refused to accept, saying: "I have already been enfeoffed as King of Qin."
translations.idiomatic: Kewang, alarmed, refused to accept, saying: "I have already been enfeoffed as King of Qin."

sentences.zh: 」畏知曰：「此偽也。

translations.literal: Weizhi said: "That is a forgery."
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi said: "That patent is a forgery."

sentences.zh: 」執恭亦曰：「彼亦偽也，所封實景國公，敕印故在。

translations.literal: Zhigong also said: "Theirs is also a forgery; what was actually granted was Duke of Jing—the patent and seal remain with us."
translations.idiomatic: Zhigong said in turn: "Theirs is forged as well. The real grant was Duke of Jing, and the patent and seal are still with us."

sentences.zh: 」可望怒，辭敕使，下畏知及執恭獄，而遣使至梧州問故，廷臣始知矯詔事。

translations.literal: Kewang was enraged, dismissed the patent envoys, imprisoned Weizhi and Zhigong, and sent an envoy to Wuzhou to inquire into the matter—the court ministers only then learned of the forged edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang flew into a rage, dismissed the patent envoys, threw Weizhi and Zhigong into prison, and sent an envoy to Wuzhou to demand an explanation—the court only then learned of the forged edicts.

sentences.zh: 文安侯馬吉翔請封可望澄江王，使者言，非「秦」不敢復命。

translations.literal: Marquis Ma Jixiang of Wen'an asked that Kewang be enfeoffed as Prince of Chengjiang; the envoy said he dared not return without the title "Qin."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jixiang, Marquis of Wen'an, proposed enfeoffing Kewang as Prince of Chengjiang; the envoy said he dared not return unless the title was "Qin."

sentences.zh: 大學士嚴起恒持不可，兵部侍郎楊鼎和助之，且請卻所獻白金玉帶。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yan Qiheng held that it should not be done; Vice Minister of War Yang Dinghe supported him and also asked that the offered gold, silver, and jade belt be refused.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yan Qiheng objected; Vice Minister of War Yang Dinghe backed him and asked that the offered gold, silver, and jade belt be refused.

sentences.zh: 會鄖國公高必正等入朝，召使者言：「本朝無異姓封王例。

translations.literal: When Duke Gao Bizheng of Ying and the rest entered court, they summoned the envoy and said: "Our dynasty has no precedent for enfeoffing non-clansmen as kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Gao Bizheng of Ying and others came to court, they summoned the envoy and said: "This dynasty has never enfeoffed a non-clansman as king.

sentences.zh: 我破京師，逼死先帝，滔天大罪，蒙恩宥赦，亦止公爵爾。

translations.literal: We stormed the capital and drove the late emperor to his death—a heaven-defying crime; though pardoned by grace, we were ennobled only as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: We stormed the capital and drove the late emperor to his death—a crime that shook heaven and earth. Though spared by grace, we were ennobled only as dukes.

sentences.zh: 張氏竊據一隅，罪固減等，封上公足矣，安敢冀王爵。

translations.literal: Zhang's band merely holds one corner; their crime is indeed lesser, and enfeoffment as supreme duke is enough—how dare they hope for a princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang holds only a corner of the realm; their guilt is the lesser sort—supreme duke is enough; how dare they aspire to a prince's title?

sentences.zh: 自今當與我同心報國，洗去賊名，毋欺朝廷孱弱，我兩家士馬足相當也。

translations.literal: From now on you should join me in loyal service to the state, wash away the name of bandit, do not bully the court's weakness, and our two hosts of men and horses are fully a match for each other.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter serve the state with one heart, shed the bandit's name, do not despise the court's frailty—our armies are evenly matched.

sentences.zh: 」又致書可望，詞義嚴正。

translations.literal: " He also wrote to Kewang in stern and upright terms.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote to Kewang in severe, upright language.

sentences.zh: 使者唯唯退，議遂寢。

translations.literal: The envoy withdrew with murmured assent and the deliberation was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy withdrew in assent and the matter died.

sentences.zh: 必正者，李自成妻弟，同陷京師者也。

translations.literal: Bizheng was Li Zicheng's brother-in-law and had entered the capital with him.
translations.idiomatic: Bizheng was Li Zicheng's brother-in-law and had shared in the fall of the capital.

sentences.zh: 可望不得封，益怒。

translations.literal: Kewang, denied enfeoffment, grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: Denied his patent, Kewang grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 其年九月親率兵至貴州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he personally led troops into Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month he led troops into Guizhou in person.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大兵破廣州、桂林，王走南寧。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the northern armies took Guangzhou and Guilin and the Prince fled to Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Qing took Guangzhou and Guilin; the Prince fled to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 事急，遣編修劉襜封可望冀王，可望仍不受。

translations.literal: The crisis urgent, he sent the compiler Liu Chan to enfeoff Kewang as Prince of Ji; Kewang still would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In extremity he sent Liu Chan to make Kewang Prince of Ji; Kewang still refused.

sentences.zh: 畏知曰：「『秦』『冀』等爾，假何如真？

translations.literal: Weizhi said: "Qin and Ji are alike—what is a false title beside a true one?
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi said: "Qin or Ji—what is a forged title next to a true one?

sentences.zh: 」可望不聽。

translations.literal: " Kewang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Kewang would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 定國等勸可望遣畏知終其事，可望許之。

translations.literal: Dingguo and the others urged Kewang to send Weizhi to finish the matter, and Kewang consented.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo urged Kewang to send Weizhi to complete the business, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年二月先遣部將賀九儀、張勝、張明誌赴南寧索沮「秦」封者起恒、鼎和及給事中劉堯珍、吳霖、張載述殺之，乃真封可望秦王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he first sent the generals He Jiuyi, Zhang Sheng, and Zhang Mingzhi to Nanning to kill those who had blocked the Qin enfeoffment—Qiheng, Dinghe, and the supervising secretaries Liu Yaozhen, Wu Lin, and Zhang Zaishu—and then truly enfeoffed Kewang as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Next year in the second month he sent He Jiuyi, Zhang Sheng, and Zhang Mingzhi to Nanning to kill Qiheng, Dinghe, Liu Yaozhen, Wu Lin, and Zhang Zaishu, who had opposed the Qin patent, and then enfeoffed Kewang as Prince of Qin in earnest.

sentences.zh: 而畏知旋至，痛哭自劾，語多侵可望。

translations.literal: When Weizhi soon arrived, he wept and memorialized impeaching himself, his words often insulting Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi arrived, wept, impeached himself, and spoke insultingly of Kewang.

sentences.zh: 遂留為東閣大學士，與吳貞毓同輔政。

translations.literal: He was retained as grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge and assisted government together with Wu Zhenyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept as Eastern Lodge grand secretary and governed with Wu Zhenyu.

sentences.zh: 可望聞之怒，使人召至貴陽，面責數之。

translations.literal: Kewang heard and was angry; he sent men to summon Weizhi to Guiyang and rebuked him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang, enraged, summoned Weizhi to Guiyang and rebuked him face to face.

sentences.zh: 畏知大憤，除頭上冠擊可望，遂被殺。

translations.literal: Weizhi in great fury took the cap from his head and struck Kewang with it, and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi snatched off his cap, struck Kewang, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 楚雄人以畏知守城功，為立祠以祀。

translations.literal: The people of Chuxiong, for Weizhi's merit in holding the city, erected a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chuxiong raised a shrine to honor his defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 吳貞毓

translations.literal: Wu Zhenyu
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhenyu

sentences.zh: 吳貞毓，字元聲，宜興人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhenyu, styled Yuansheng, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhenyu, style name Yuansheng, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Chongzhen 16.

sentences.zh: 事唐王為吏部文選主事。

translations.literal: He served the Prince of Tang as director of the Civil Appointment Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Tang he was director of civil appointments in Personnel.

sentences.zh: 事敗，擁立永明王，進郎中。

translations.literal: When that cause failed he installed the Prince of Yongming and was promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fell he installed the Prince of Yongming and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 王駐全州，加太常少卿，仍掌選事。

translations.literal: When the Prince was at Quanzhou, Zhenyu was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while still directing appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At Quanzhou he became vice director of Imperial Sacrifices while keeping appointments.

sentences.zh: 已，擢吏部右侍郎，從至肇慶，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to right vice minister of Personnel, followed to Zhaoqing, and was made minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice minister of Personnel, went to Zhaoqing, and was made minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 廣東、西會城先後失，王徙潯州，再徒南寧，貞毓並從。

translations.literal: The capitals of Guangdong and Guangxi fell in turn; the Prince moved to Xunzhou and again to Nanning, and Zhenyu followed throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong and Guangxi fell; the Prince moved to Xunzhou and Nanning, and Zhenyu followed.

sentences.zh: 貞毓與嚴起恒共阻孫可望秦王封，可望殺起恒，貞毓以奉使獲免。

translations.literal: Zhenyu with Yan Qiheng together blocked Sun Kewang's patent as Prince of Qin; Kewang killed Qiheng, and Zhenyu escaped because he was on a mission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu and Yan Qiheng blocked Kewang's Qin patent; Kewang killed Qiheng; Zhenyu was spared on a mission.

sentences.zh: 及還，進東閣大學士，代起恒。

translations.literal: On his return he was advanced to grand secretary of the Eastern Lodge in Qiheng's place.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he became Eastern Lodge grand secretary in Qiheng's place.

sentences.zh: 可望自雲南遷貴陽，議移王自近，挾以作威。

translations.literal: Kewang moved from Yunnan to Guiyang and planned to move the Prince nearer to wield power through him.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang moved to Guiyang and meant to bring the Prince close and rule through him.

sentences.zh: 其將掌塘報者曹延生惎貞毓，言不可移黔。

translations.literal: His officer in charge of courier reports, Cao Yansheng, envied Zhenyu and said the Prince must not be moved to Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yansheng, who handled courier reports, envied Zhenyu and warned against moving the court to Qian.

sentences.zh: 時順治八年，大兵南征，勢日迫。

translations.literal: It was the eighth year of Shunzhi; the northern armies marched south and the pressure grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 the Qing advanced south and danger tightened daily.

sentences.zh: 王召諸臣議，有請走海濱就李元胤者，有議入安南避難者，有議泛海抵閩依鄭成功者。

translations.literal: The Prince summoned the ministers to deliberate; some asked to flee to the seacoast and join Li Yuanyin, some proposed entering Annam for refuge, some urged crossing the sea to Fujian to rely on Zheng Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince called council; some urged the coast and Li Yuanyin, some Annam, some Zheng Chenggong in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 惟馬吉翔、龐天壽結可望，堅主赴黔。

translations.literal: Only Ma Jixiang and Pang Tianshou, allied with Kewang, firmly urged going to Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ma Jixiang and Pang Tianshou, tied to Kewang, insisted on Qian.

sentences.zh: 貞毓因前阻封議，且入延生言，不敢決。

translations.literal: Zhenyu, because of his earlier opposition to the patent and Yansheng's words, dared not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu, having blocked the patent and heeding Yansheng, could not decide.

sentences.zh: 元胤疏請出海。

translations.literal: Yuanyin memorialized asking to go to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyin asked to take the court to sea.

sentences.zh: 王不欲就可望，而以海濱遠，再下廷議，終不決。

translations.literal: The Prince did not wish to submit to Kewang, yet the seacoast was far; he ordered debate again and in the end could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince shrank from Kewang but found the sea too distant; debate continued without decision.

sentences.zh: 亡何，開國公趙印選、衛國公胡一青殿後軍，戰敗奔還。
