translations.literal: Before long the founding duke Zhao Yinxuan and the defending duke Hu Yiqing, rearguard troops, were defeated and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao Yinxuan and Hu Yiqing were beaten on the rearguard and fled back.

sentences.zh: 請王速行，急由水道走土司，抵瀨湍。

translations.literal: They begged the Prince to flee at once, urgently taking the water route through tribal territory to Laituan.
translations.idiomatic: They begged the Prince to flee at once by water through tribal lands to Laituan.

sentences.zh: 二將報大兵益近，相距止百里。

translations.literal: The two generals reported that the northern armies drew nearer, only a hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: They reported the Qing only a hundred li behind.

sentences.zh: 上下失色，皆散去。

translations.literal: High and low turned pale and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Court and camp panicked and scattered.

sentences.zh: 已，次羅江土司，追騎相距止一舍。

translations.literal: Later they halted at the Luojiang tribal domain; pursuing horsemen were only one stage behind.
translations.idiomatic: At Luojiang the pursuers were a single stage behind.

sentences.zh: 會日晡引去，乃稍安。

translations.literal: At dusk they withdrew, and all grew somewhat calmer.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the pursuers drew off and fear eased.

sentences.zh: 次龍英，抵廣南，歲己暮。

translations.literal: They next reached Longying and arrived at Guangnan as the year ended.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Longying and Guangnan as the year closed.

sentences.zh: 可望遣兵以明年二月迎王入安隆所，改為安龍府，奉王居之。

translations.literal: Kewang sent troops to welcome the Prince in the second month of the following year into Anlong prefecture, renamed Anlong fu, and lodged the Prince there.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang welcomed the Prince in the second month to Anlong, renamed Anlong fu, and housed him there.

sentences.zh: 宮室庳陋，服禦粗惡，守護將悖逆無人臣禮，王不堪其憂。

translations.literal: The palace was low and mean, dress and food coarse and vile; the guarding generals were insolent without the manners of subjects, and the Prince could not bear the grief.
translations.idiomatic: The palace was squalid, provisions mean, guards insolent—the Prince lived in misery.

sentences.zh: 吉翔掌戎政，天壽督勇衛營，諂事可望，謀禪代。

translations.literal: Jixiang held military affairs and Tianshou commanded the Brave Guard camp; they flattered Kewang and plotted abdication in his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang ran the army, Tianshou the Brave Guard; they fawned on Kewang and plotted usurpation.

sentences.zh: 惡貞毓不附己，令其黨冷孟銋、吳象元、方祚亨交章彈擊。

translations.literal: Hating that Zhenyu would not join them, they had their partisans Leng Mengyin, Wu Xiangyuan, and Fang Zuheng impeach him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They set their men Leng Mengyin, Wu Xiangyuan, and Fang Zuheng to impeach Zhenyu.

sentences.zh: 且語孟銋等曰：「秦王宰天下，我具啟，以內外事盡付戎政、勇衛二司。

translations.literal: They also told Mengyin and the rest: "The Prince of Qin rules all under Heaven; I shall memorialize to entrust inner and outer affairs entirely to the military administration and Brave Guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: They said: "When the Prince of Qin rules, I will give all affairs to military administration and the Brave Guard.

sentences.zh: 大權歸我，公等為羽翼，貞毓何能為！

translations.literal: Great power will return to me and you will be my wings—what can Zhenyu do!
translations.idiomatic: Power will be mine and you my wings—what can Zhenyu do!

sentences.zh: 」吉翔遂遣門生郭璘說主事胡士瑞擁戴秦王。

translations.literal: " Jixiang then sent his student Guo Lin to persuade the director Hu Shirui to support the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: " Jixiang sent Guo Lin to win Hu Shirui for the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 士瑞怒，歷聲叱退之。

translations.literal: Shirui in anger shouted him down and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Shirui shouted him down and expelled him.

sentences.zh: 他日，吉翔遣璘求郎中古其品畫《堯舜禪受圖》以獻可望，其品拒不從。

translations.literal: Another day Jixiang sent Lin to ask the bureau director Gu Qipin to paint "Yao and Shun's Abdication" to present to Kewang; Qipin refused.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang later asked Gu Qipin to paint Yao and Shun's abdication for Kewang; Qipin refused.

sentences.zh: 吉翔譖於可望，杖殺其品，而可望果以朝事盡委吉翔、天壽。

translations.literal: Jixiang slandered him to Kewang, who had Qipin beaten to death, and Kewang truly entrusted all court affairs to Jixiang and Tianshou.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang slandered Qipin, who was beaten to death; Kewang gave court affairs to Jixiang and Tianshou.

sentences.zh: 於是士瑞與給事中徐極，員外郎林青陽、蔡縯，主事張鐫連章發其奸謀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shirui with the supervising secretary Xu Ji, the bureau directors Lin Qingyang and Cai Yan, and the director Zhang Juan jointly exposed their treacherous plot.
translations.idiomatic: Shirui, Xu Ji, Lin Qingyang, Cai Yan, and Zhang Juan exposed the plot in joint memorials.

sentences.zh: 王大怒。

translations.literal: The Prince was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was furious.

sentences.zh: 兩人求救於太后，乃免。

translations.literal: The two men begged help from the empress dowager and were spared.
translations.idiomatic: They appealed to the empress dowager and were spared.

sentences.zh: 前御史任僎、中書方於宣勸可望設內閣九卿科道官，改印交為八疊，盡易其舊，立太廟，定朝儀，擬改國號曰：「後明」，日夕謀篡位。

translations.literal: The former censor Ren Fu and the secretarial attendant Fang Yuxuan urged Kewang to set up the inner court with the Nine Ministers and censorate officials, change the seals to eight folds, replace all the old ones, establish the imperial temple, fix court ritual, and plan to change the dynastic title to "Later Ming," plotting usurpation day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu and Fang Yuxuan urged Kewang to create ministries, change seals, establish rites, rename the state Later Ming, and seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 王聞憂懼，密謂中官張福祿、全為國曰：「聞晉王李定國已定廣西，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: The Prince heard and was fearful; he secretly told the eunuchs Zhang Fulu and Quan Weiguo: "I hear Prince Jin Li Dingguo has settled Guangxi and his army's fame rises greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince secretly told eunuchs Zhang Fulu and Quan Weiguo: "Prince Jin Li Dingguo has taken Guangxi; his fame resounds.

sentences.zh: 欲密下一敕，令統兵入衛。

translations.literal: I wish secretly to issue an edict ordering him to lead troops to guard me.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to send a secret order for him to march to my guard.

sentences.zh: 若等能密圖乎？

translations.literal: Can you plot this in secret?
translations.idiomatic: Can you arrange this in secret?

sentences.zh: 」二人言徐極、林青陽、張鐫、蔡縯、胡士瑞曾疏劾吉翔、天壽，宜可與謀，王即令告之。

translations.literal: " The two said that Xu Ji, Lin Qingyang, Zhang Juan, Cai Yan, and Hu Shirui had memorialized against Jixiang and Tianshou and could be trusted; the Prince at once had them told.
translations.idiomatic: " They named Xu Ji, Lin Qingyang, Zhang Juan, Cai Yan, and Hu Shirui, and the Prince sent word.

sentences.zh: 五人許諾，引以告貞毓。

translations.literal: The five promised and led them to tell Zhenyu.
translations.idiomatic: The five agreed and informed Zhenyu.

sentences.zh: 貞毓曰：「主上憂危，正我輩報國之秋。

translations.literal: Zhenyu said: "The sovereign's peril is exactly our season to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu said: "The throne in peril is our time to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 諸君中誰能充此使者？

translations.literal: Which of you gentlemen can be the envoy?
translations.idiomatic: Who among you can go as envoy?

sentences.zh: 」青陽請行。

translations.literal: " Qingyang volunteered.
translations.idiomatic: " Qingyang volunteered.

sentences.zh: 乃令佯乞假歸葬，而使員外郎蔣乾昌撰予定國敕，主事朱東旦書之，福祿等持入用寶。

translations.literal: They then had him pretend to ask leave for burial while the bureau director Jiang Ganchang drafted the edict for Dingguo, the director Zhu Dongdan wrote it, and Fulu and the rest carried it in to be sealed.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned a funeral leave while Jiang Ganchang drafted the edict, Zhu Dongdan wrote it, and the eunuchs sealed it.

sentences.zh: 青陽於歲盡間道馳至定國所。

translations.literal: At year's end Qingyang raced by secret paths to Dingguo's camp.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end Qingyang reached Dingguo by hidden routes.

sentences.zh: 定國接敕感泣，許以迎王。

translations.literal: Dingguo received the edict, wept with emotion, and promised to welcome the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo wept on receiving the edict and promised to rescue the Prince.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，青陽久未還，王將擇使往促，貞毓以翰林孔目周官對。

translations.literal: The next summer Qingyang had long not returned; the Prince would choose an envoy to urge him on, and Zhenyu named the Hanlin registrar Zhou Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Next summer, with Qingyang long absent, Zhenyu named Zhou Guan as envoy.

sentences.zh: 都督鄭胤元曰：「吉翔晨夕在側，假他事出之外，庶有濟。

translations.literal: The regional commander Zheng Yinyuan said: "Jixiang is at the Prince's side morning and night; send him away on some other business and there may be hope.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yinyuan said: "Send Jixiang away on pretense and we may succeed.

sentences.zh: 」王乃令吉翔奉使祭先王及王太后陵於梧州、南寧，而遣周官詣定國。

translations.literal: " The Prince then ordered Jixiang to go on mission to sacrifice at the tombs of the former prince and empress dowager at Wuzhou and Nanning, and sent Zhou Guan to Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince sent Jixiang to sacrifice at Wuzhou and Nanning and Zhou Guan to Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 吉翔在道，微知青陽密敕事，遣人至定國營偵之。

translations.literal: On the road Jixiang faintly learned of Qingyang's secret edict and sent men to spy on Dingguo's camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Jixiang learned of the secret edict and spied on Dingguo's camp.

sentences.zh: 主事劉議新者，道遇吉翔，意其必預謀也，告以兩使賫敕狀。

translations.literal: The director Liu Yixin, meeting Jixiang on the way, thought he must be in the plot and told him both envoys bore edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yixin met Jixiang and, thinking him in the plot, told of both envoys and the edicts.

sentences.zh: 吉翔驚駭，啟報可望。

translations.literal: Jixiang was shocked and reported to Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang reported to Kewang in alarm.

sentences.zh: 可望大怒，並疑吉翔預謀，遣其將鄭國赴南寧逮之。

translations.literal: Kewang was greatly angered and suspected Jixiang of complicity too; he sent his general Zheng Guo to Nanning to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang raged, suspected Jixiang, and sent Zheng Guo to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 會鐫、士瑞及李元開以王親試，極、縯、東旦及御史林鍾以久次，皆予美官。

translations.literal: Just then Juan, Shirui, and Li Yuankai received high offices for the Prince's kin examination, and Ji, Yan, Dongdan, and the censor Lin Zhong for long seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Juan, Shirui, and Li Yuankai won posts in the kin exam; Ji, Yan, Dongdan, and Lin Zhong for seniority.

sentences.zh: 天壽及吉翔弟都督雄飛忌甚，與其黨郭璘方謀陷之。

translations.literal: Tianshou and Jixiang's brother the regional commander Xiongfei hated this deeply and with Guo Lin plotted their ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou and Xiongfei plotted with Guo Lin against them.

sentences.zh: 而鍾、縯、極、鐫、士瑞亦知事泄，倉皇劾吉翔、天壽表裏為奸。

translations.literal: Zhong, Yan, Ji, Juan, and Shirui, knowing the affair was exposed, hurriedly impeached Jixiang and Tianshou as partners in crime.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing exposure, Zhong, Yan, Ji, Juan, and Shirui impeached Jixiang and Tianshou.

sentences.zh: 王見事急，即下廷臣議罪。

translations.literal: The Prince, seeing matters urgent, at once ordered the court to deliberate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince ordered the court to judge the case.

sentences.zh: 天壽懼，與雄飛馳貴陽，告可望。

translations.literal: Tianshou in fear with Xiongfei raced to Guiyang and told Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou fled with Xiongfei to Guiyang and informed Kewang.

sentences.zh: 初，青陽還至南寧，為守將常榮所留，密遣親信劉吉告之王。

translations.literal: Earlier Qingyang had returned to Nanning and was detained by the garrison commander Chang Rong, who secretly sent his confidant Liu Ji to inform the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyang had returned to Nanning; Chang Rong detained him but Liu Ji warned the Prince.

sentences.zh: 王喜，改青陽給事中，諭貞毓再撰敕，鑄「屏翰親臣」金印，令吉還付青陽。

translations.literal: The Prince rejoiced, made Qingyang a supervising secretary, and ordered Zhenyu to draft another edict and cast the gold seal "Pillar and Kin of the Throne" for Ji to deliver to Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince made Qingyang supervising secretary and ordered a new edict and the gold seal "Pillar and Kin" for Ji to carry to Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 至廉州，周官與青陽遇，偕至高州賜定國，定國拜受命。

translations.literal: At Lianzhou, Zhou Guan met Qingyang; together they went to Gaozhou to invest Dingguo, who bowed and accepted command.
translations.idiomatic: At Lianzhou Zhou Guan met Qingyang; at Gaozhou Dingguo accepted the commission.

sentences.zh: 而是時鄭國已械吉翔至安龍，與諸臣面質。

translations.literal: By then Zheng Guo had already shackled Jixiang and brought him to Anlong to confront the ministers face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guo had shackled Jixiang at Anlong for confrontation.

sentences.zh: 貞毓謝不知，國怒，因挾貞毓直入王所居文華殿，迫脅王，索主謀者。

translations.literal: Zhenyu pleaded ignorance; Guo in anger seized Zhenyu and entered the Wenhua Hall where the Prince lived, coercing the Prince to name the chief plotters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu denied knowledge; Guo dragged him into the Wenhua Hall and forced the Prince to name conspirators.

sentences.zh: 王懼，不敢正言，謂必外人假敕寶為之。

translations.literal: The Prince in fear dared not speak plainly and said outsiders must have forged the edict and seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince, afraid, said outsiders must have forged edict and seal.

sentences.zh: 國遂努目出，與天壽至朝房，械貞毓並胤元、鍾、縯、乾昌、元開、極、鐫、士瑞、東旦及太僕少卿趙賡禹，御史周允吉、朱議篸，員外郎任鬥墟，主事易士佳系私室。

translations.literal: Guo glared and went out with Tianshou to the court offices, shackling Zhenyu together with Yinyuan, Zhong, Yan, Ganchang, Yuankai, Ji, Juan, Shirui, Dongdan, and the vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Zhao Gengyu, the censors Zhou Yunji and Zhu Yicen, the bureau director Ren Douxu, and the director Yi Shijia in a private room.
translations.idiomatic: Guo shackled Zhenyu, Yinyuan, Zhong, Yan, Ganchang, Yuankai, Ji, Juan, Shirui, Dongdan, Zhao Gengyu, Zhou Yunji, Zhu Yicen, Ren Douxu, and Yi Shijia.

sentences.zh: 又入宮擒福祿、為國而出。

translations.literal: He again entered the palace and seized Fulu and Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Fulu and Weiguo from the palace.

sentences.zh: 其黨冷孟銋、蒲纓、宋德亮、朱企鋘等迫王速具主名，王悲憤而退。

translations.literal: Leng Mengyin, Pu Ying, Song Deliang, Zhu Qimao, and the rest pressed the Prince to name the principals quickly; the Prince withdrew in grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyin, Pu Ying, Song Deliang, and Zhu Qimao pressed the Prince for names; he withdrew in grief.

sentences.zh: 翊日，國等嚴刑拷掠，獨貞毓以大臣免。

translations.literal: The next day Guo and the rest tortured them severely; only Zhenyu as a great minister was exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they tortured all but Zhenyu as a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 眾不勝楚，大呼二祖列宗，且大罵。

translations.literal: The others could not bear the pain, cried out to the founding ancestors, and cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The rest cried to the ancestors and cursed under torture.

sentences.zh: 時日已暮，風雷忽震烈。

translations.literal: Evening came and wind and thunder suddenly shook violently.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk wind and thunder shook violently.

sentences.zh: 縯厲聲曰：「今日縯等直承此獄，稍見臣子報國苦衷。

translations.literal: Yan cried out loudly: "Today Yan and the rest openly accept this case, that the loyal grief of subjects may be seen a little.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yan cried: "Today we openly bear this charge, that our loyalty may be seen.

sentences.zh: 」由是眾皆自承。

translations.literal: " Thereupon all confessed of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " Then all confessed.

sentences.zh: 國又問曰：「主上知否？

translations.literal: Guo again asked: "Did the sovereign know?
translations.idiomatic: Guo asked: "Did the Prince know?

sentences.zh: 」縯大聲曰：「未經奏明。

translations.literal: " Yan cried loudly: "It was not yet reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan shouted: "He was not yet told.

sentences.zh: 」乃復收繫，以欺君誤國盜寶矯詔為罪，報可望。

translations.literal: " They were imprisoned again, charged with deceiving the ruler, harming the state, stealing the seal, and forging edicts, and reported to Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: " They were charged with deceiving the ruler, forging edicts, and stealing the seal, and reported to Kewang.

sentences.zh: 可望請王親裁，王不勝憤，下廷議。

translations.literal: Kewang asked the Prince to judge in person; the Prince, unable to bear his anger, ordered court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang asked the Prince to judge; the Prince ordered court debate.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎張佐辰及纓、德亮、孟銋、企鋘、蔣御曦等謂國曰：「此輩盡當處死。

translations.literal: The vice minister Zhang Zuochen and Pu Ying, Deliang, Mengyin, Qimao, Jiang Yuxi, and the rest told Guo: "These men must all be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zuochen, Pu Ying, Deliang, Mengyin, Qimao, and Jiang Yuxi urged death for all.

sentences.zh: 儻留一人，將為後患。

translations.literal: If one is left, he will be a future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Leave one alive and he will be a future scourge.

sentences.zh: 」於是御曦執筆，佐辰擬旨，以鐫、福祿、為國為首罪，淩遲，餘為從罪，斬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuxi took up the brush and Zuochen drafted the rescript: Juan, Fulu, and Weiguo as principal culprits were to suffer lingering death; the rest were accomplices to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi wrote and Zuochen drafted the sentence: Juan, Fulu, and Weiguo were to die by lingering execution; the rest by beheading.

sentences.zh: 王以貞毓大臣，言於可望罪絞。

translations.literal: The Prince, because Zhenyu was a great minister, spoke to Kewang that the crime warranted strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said Zhenyu, as a great minister, deserved strangulation.

sentences.zh: 吉翔以福祿等內侍，謂王后知情，將廢之，令主事蕭尹歷陳古廢后事。

translations.literal: Jixiang, because Fulu and the rest were inner attendants, said the empress knew and would be deposed; he ordered the director Xiao Yin to enumerate ancient cases of deposed empresses.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang claimed the empress knew and must be deposed; Xiao Yin recited precedents of deposed empresses.

sentences.zh: 後泣訴於王，乃已。

translations.literal: The empress wept and pleaded to the Prince, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept to the Prince and the matter stopped.

sentences.zh: 諸人就刑，神色不變，各賦詩大罵而死。

translations.literal: As the condemned went to execution their expressions did not change; each composed a poem and died cursing.
translations.idiomatic: They went to death unflinching, each composing a poem and cursing to the end.

sentences.zh: 其家人合瘞於安龍北關之馬場。

translations.literal: Their families buried them together at the horse ground outside Anlong's north gate.
translations.idiomatic: Their families buried them together at the horse ground north of Anlong.

sentences.zh: 已而青陽逮至，亦被殺，獨官走免。

translations.literal: Before long Qingyang was seized and also killed; only Guan escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyang was seized and killed; only Zhou Guan escaped.

sentences.zh: 時順治十一年三月也。

translations.literal: It was the third month of the eleventh year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was the third month of Shunzhi 11.

sentences.zh: 居二載，定國竟奉前敕護王入雲南。

translations.literal: Two years later Dingguo at last obeyed the earlier edict and escorted the Prince into Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Dingguo escorted the Prince into Yunnan under the old edict.

sentences.zh: 乃贈貞毓少師、太子太師、吏部尚書、中極殿大學士，賜祭，謚文忠，蔭子錦衣，世千戶，餘贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Zhenyu was posthumously made junior tutor, grand tutor of the heir apparent, minister of Personnel, and grand secretary of the Central Pole Hall, granted sacrifice, given the posthumous name Wenzhong, and his son ennobled as hereditary commander of the embroidered guard for a thousand households; the rest received posthumous favors by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu was posthumously honored as tutor, minister, and grand secretary Wenzhong; his son received a hereditary guard command; others were mourned by rank.

sentences.zh: 已，建廟於馬場，勒碑大書「十八先生成仁處」以旌其忠。

translations.literal: Later a temple was built at the horse ground and a stele carved in large characters "Place where the Eighteen Masters achieved martyrdom" to honor their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: A temple and stele "Where the Eighteen Masters achieved martyrdom" were raised at the horse ground.

sentences.zh: 定國既奉王居滇，即捕吉翔及其家人，令部將靳統武收系，將殺之。

translations.literal: After Dingguo lodged the Prince in Yunnan, he at once arrested Jixiang and his family and ordered the commander Jin Tongwu to imprison them for execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan Dingguo arrested Jixiang's household and ordered Jin Tongwu to hold them for execution.

sentences.zh: 吉翔日媚統武，定國客詣統武，吉翔復媚之。

translations.literal: Jixiang daily flattered Tongwu; when Dingguo's clients visited Tongwu, Jixiang flattered them too.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang fawned on Tongwu and on Dingguo's clients.

sentences.zh: 因相與譽吉翔於定國，而微為辨冤。

translations.literal: They praised Jixiang to Dingguo together and subtly pleaded his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Together they praised Jixiang to Dingguo and pleaded his case.

sentences.zh: 定國召吉翔，吉翔入謁，即叩頭言：「王再造功，千古無兩。

translations.literal: Dingguo summoned Jixiang; on entering audience Jixiang at once kowtowed and said: "Your Highness's merit in restoring the dynasty is unmatched in a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo summoned him; Jixiang kowtowed and praised his restoration of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 吉翔幸望見顏色，死且不朽，他是非，何足辨也。

translations.literal: Jixiang is fortunate to behold your countenance; though I die I shall not perish—other rights and wrongs are not worth arguing.
translations.idiomatic: To see your face is honor enough; other charges are nothing.

sentences.zh: 」定國乃大喜。

translations.literal: " Dingguo was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Dingguo was delighted.

sentences.zh: 吉翔因日諂定國客，令說定國薦己入內閣，遂與定國客蟠結，盡握中外權，天壽亦復用事。

translations.literal: Jixiang therefore daily flattered Dingguo's clients, had them urge Dingguo to recommend him to the inner cabinet, knotted himself with Dingguo's clients, grasped all power inside and out, and Tianshou too returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: He flattered Dingguo's clients, entered the cabinet, seized power, and Tianshou returned to office.

sentences.zh: 後從王入緬甸，天壽先死，吉翔為緬人所殺。

translations.literal: Later following the Prince into Burma, Tianshou died first and Jixiang was killed by the Burmese.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Prince into Burma, Tianshou died first; the Burmese killed Jixiang.

sentences.zh: 高勣，字無功，紹興人。

translations.literal: Gao Ji, styled Wugong, was a native of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ji, style name Wugong, came from Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 事永明王，歷官光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He served the Prince of Yongming and rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Prince of Yongming as vice director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 馬吉翔、龐天壽構殺吳貞毓等，李定國奉王至雲南，捕吉翔將殺之。

translations.literal: Ma Jixiang and Pang Tianshou framed and killed Wu Zhenyu and the rest; Li Dingguo brought the Prince to Yunnan, arrested Jixiang, and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang and Tianshou destroyed Wu Zhenyu; Dingguo arrested Jixiang in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 已，為其所諛，遂免死，且薦入閣，遂得盡握中外權，而天壽亦用事。

translations.literal: Already he had been won by flattery, spared death, and even recommended to the inner cabinet; he grasped all power inside and out, and Tianshou too held office.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery spared Jixiang; he entered the cabinet and ruled inside and out with Tianshou.

sentences.zh: 定國與劉文秀時詣二人家，定國時封晉王，文秀蜀王也。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Liu Wenxiu often visited the two men's houses; Dingguo was then Prince of Jin and Wenxiu Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo, Prince of Jin, and Wenxiu, Prince of Shu, often visited them.

sentences.zh: 勣與御史鄔昌期患之，合疏言二人功高望重，不當往來權佞之門，恐滋奸弊，復蹈秦王故轍。

translations.literal: Ji with the censor Wu Changqi feared this, jointly memorializing that the two men's merit and standing were high and they should not frequent the doors of powerful flatterers, lest corruption grow and they tread the Prince of Qin's old path.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Censor Wu Changqi memorialized that the princes should not court corrupt favorites lest history repeat.

sentences.zh: 疏上，二王遂不入朝。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the two princes ceased attending court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial submitted, both princes stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 吉翔激王怒，命各杖一百五十，除名。

translations.literal: Jixiang provoked the Prince's anger and ordered each beaten one hundred fifty strokes and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang stirred the Prince's wrath; each was beaten one hundred fifty strokes and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 定國客金維新走告定國曰：「勣等誠有罪，但不可有殺諫官名。

translations.literal: Dingguo's client Jin Weixin ran to tell Dingguo: "Ji and the rest are indeed guilty, but you must not earn the name of killing remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Weixin warned Dingguo: "Do not be known for killing remonstrators."

sentences.zh: 」定國即偕文秀入救，乃復官。

translations.literal: Dingguo at once went with Wenxiu to intercede, and their offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu interceded and their posts were restored.

sentences.zh: 及定國敗孫可望兵，自以為無他患，武備盡弛。

translations.literal: After Dingguo defeated Sun Kewang's army he thought himself free of other troubles and military preparations were wholly relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Kewang, Dingguo relaxed all military preparations.

sentences.zh: 勣與郎官金簡進諫曰：「今內難雖除，外憂方大。

translations.literal: Ji with the court gentleman Jin Jian remonstrated: "Though inner trouble is removed, outer peril is great.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Jin Jian remonstrated: "Inner foes are gone, outer peril remains.

sentences.zh: 伺我者頓刃待兩虎之斃，而我酣歌漏舟之中，熟寢爇薪之上，能旦夕安耶？

translations.literal: Those who watch us sharpen blades waiting for two tigers to perish, while we sing drunken in a leaking boat and sleep sound on burning firewood—can we be at ease even for a morning and evening?
translations.idiomatic: Our enemies wait for us to exhaust each other while we feast in a leaking boat on burning coals—can we rest?

sentences.zh: 二王老於兵事，胡泄泄如死。

translations.literal: The two princes are old in military affairs—why are they as heedless as dead men?
translations.idiomatic: You are veterans of war—why so heedless?

sentences.zh: 」定國之王前，頗激。

translations.literal: Dingguo before the Prince was somewhat stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo was stung before the Prince.

sentences.zh: 王擬杖二臣以解之，朝士多爭不可，移時未能決。

translations.literal: The Prince planned to beat the two ministers to settle it; courtiers for a long time disputed that it could not be done and for a time could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince would punish them; courtiers long disputed until no decision came.

sentences.zh: 而三路敗書至，定國始逡巡引謝，二臣獲免。

translations.literal: Then reports of defeat on three routes arrived and Dingguo hesitantly withdrew his blame; the two ministers were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat on three fronts came; Dingguo relented and the ministers were spared.

sentences.zh: 簡，字萬藏，勣鄉人。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Wanzang, was Ji's townsman.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, style Wanzang, was Ji's townsman.

sentences.zh: 後王入緬甸，二人扈行，並死之。

translations.literal: Later when the Prince entered Burma the two men followed and both died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince entered Burma both followed and died.

sentences.zh: 有李如月者，東莞人，官御史。

translations.literal: There was Li Ruyue, a native of Dongguan, who held the office of censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruyue of Dongguan was a censor.

sentences.zh: 王駐安龍時，孫可望獲叛將陳邦傳父子，去其皮，傳屍至安龍。

translations.literal: When the Prince was at Anlong, Sun Kewang captured the rebel Chen Bangchuan and his son, flayed them, and sent the corpses to Anlong.
translations.idiomatic: At Anlong, Kewang flayed Chen Bangchuan and his son and sent the bodies thither.

sentences.zh: 如月劾可望不請旨，擅殺勛鎮，罪同莽、操，而請加邦傳惡謚，以懲不忠。

translations.literal: Ruyue impeached Kewang for not requesting orders and killing a meritorious commander on his own authority, a crime like Wang Mang and Cao Cao, and asked that a posthumous name of infamy be added to Bangchuan to punish disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyue impeached Kewang for killing a commander without warrant, likening him to Wang Mang and Cao Cao, and asked an infamous posthumous title for Bangchuan.

sentences.zh: 王知可望必怒，留其疏。

translations.literal: The Prince knew Kewang would surely be angry and kept the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince, knowing Kewang's wrath, withheld the memorial.

sentences.zh: 召如月入，諭以謚本褒忠，無惡謚理。

translations.literal: He summoned Ruyue in and instructed him that posthumous names honor the loyal; there is no principle of infamous titles.
translations.idiomatic: He told Ruyue posthumous names praise loyalty, not infamy.

sentences.zh: 小臣妄言亂制，杖四十，除名，意將解可望。

translations.literal: A petty official's reckless words disturb the system—forty strokes and removal from office, intending to appease Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Ruyue forty strokes and dismissed him to appease Kewang.

sentences.zh: 而可望大怒，遣人至王所，執如月至朝門外，抑使跪。

translations.literal: Yet Kewang was greatly angry, sent men to the Prince's place, seized Ruyue before the court gate, and forced him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang was still furious, seized Ruyue at the gate, and forced him to kneel.

sentences.zh: 如月向闕叩頭，大呼太祖高皇帝，極口大罵。

translations.literal: Ruyue kowtowed toward the palace, cried out "Great Emperor Taizu of the founding line," and cursed with all his might.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyue kowtowed toward the palace, cried "Taizu," and cursed without cease.

sentences.zh: 其人遂剔其皮，斷手足及首，實草皮內紉之，懸於通衢。

translations.literal: The men then flayed him, cut off hands, feet, and head, stuffed the skin with straw, sewed it, and hung it in the public way.
translations.idiomatic: They flayed him, severed limbs and head, stuffed the skin with straw, and hung it in the street.

sentences.zh: 又有任國璽者，官行人。

translations.literal: There was also Ren Guoxi, who held the office of bearer of decrees.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Guoxi was a bearer of decrees.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年，永明王將出奔，國璽獨請死守。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, as the Prince of Yongming was about to flee, Guoxi alone asked to hold the city and die.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15, as the Prince would flee, Guoxi alone asked to hold and die.

sentences.zh: 章下廷議，李定國等言：「行人議是。

translations.literal: The memorial went to court debate; Li Dingguo and the rest said: "The bearer's proposal is right.
translations.idiomatic: At court Dingguo said: "The bearer is right.

sentences.zh: 但前途尚寬，暫移蹕，卷土重來，再圖恢復，未晚也。

translations.literal: But the road ahead is still wide; move the throne for a time, gather strength and return, and plan recovery—it is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the road remains open; withdraw for a time, gather strength, and restore the realm—not too late.

sentences.zh: 」乃扈王入緬甸。

translations.literal: " They then escorted the Prince into Burma.
translations.idiomatic: " They escorted the Prince into Burma.

sentences.zh: 緬俗以中秋日大會群蠻，令黔國公沐天波偕諸酋椎髻跣足，以臣禮見。

translations.literal: Burmese custom on the mid-autumn festival gathers the tribes; they ordered the Duke of Qian Mu Tianbo together with the chiefs to wear matted hair and bare feet and meet them with the ritual of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: At mid-autumn the Burmese made Mu Tianbo and the chiefs attend barefoot with subject ritual.

sentences.zh: 天波不得已從之，歸泣告眾曰：「我所以屈辱者，懼驚憂主上耳。

translations.literal: Tianbo had no choice but to comply; returning he wept and told the assembly: "The reason I endured humiliation was fear of alarming and grieving the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbo complied, then wept: "I endured humiliation lest the Prince be distressed.

sentences.zh: 否則彼將無狀，我罪益大。

translations.literal: Otherwise they would have acted without restraint and my guilt would have been greater.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they would have run wild and my guilt would be greater.

sentences.zh: 」國璽與禮部侍郎楊在抗疏劾之。

translations.literal: " Guoxi with the vice minister of Rites Yang Zai memorialized impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: " Guoxi and Yang Zai impeached this.

sentences.zh: 時龐天壽已死，李國泰代掌司禮監印，吉翔復與表裏為奸。

translations.literal: By then Pang Tianshou was dead and Li Guotai held the seal of the Directorate of Ceremonies; Jixiang again worked with him in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou was dead; Li Guotai held the ceremonial seal; Jixiang conspired with him.

sentences.zh: 國璽集宋末大臣賢奸事為一書，進之王，吉翔深恨之。

translations.literal: Guoxi compiled the worthy and wicked among Song-dynasty great ministers into one book and presented it to the Prince; Jixiang hated this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxi presented a book on Song ministers worthy and wicked; Jixiang hated it.

sentences.zh: 王覽止一日，國泰即竊去。

translations.literal: The Prince read it only one day and Guotai stole it away.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince read it one day; Guotai stole it.

sentences.zh: 國璽尋進御史，疏論時事三不可解，中言禍急然眉，當思出險。

translations.literal: Guoxi soon advanced to censor and memorialized on current affairs with three things beyond explanation, saying calamity pressed on the brow and one must think how to escape danger.
translations.idiomatic: As censor Guoxi said three things were inexplicable and calamity pressed on the brow—escape was needed.

sentences.zh: 吉翔不悅，即令國璽獻出險策。

translations.literal: Jixiang was displeased and at once ordered Guoxi to present a plan to escape danger.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang ordered him to present an escape plan.

sentences.zh: 國璽忿然曰：「時事至此，猶抑言官使不言耶！」

translations.literal: Guoxi angrily said: "When affairs have come to this, will you still suppress the censorate and forbid speech!"
translations.idiomatic: Guoxi cried: "And you still silence the censorate!"

sentences.zh: 時緬甸弟弒兄自立，欲盡殺文武諸臣，遣人來言曰：「蠻俗貴詛盟，請與天朝諸公飲咒水。

translations.literal: At that time a younger brother in Burma murdered his elder brother and seized the throne, wishing to kill all civil and military ministers; he sent men saying: "Barbarian custom honors oath by curse; please drink oath-water with the gentlemen of the heavenly court."
translations.idiomatic: A Burmese prince murdered his brother and meant to kill all Ming ministers, inviting them to drink oath-water.

sentences.zh: 」吉翔、國泰邀諸臣盡往。

translations.literal: Jixiang and Guotai invited all the ministers to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang and Guotai invited all ministers.

sentences.zh: 至則以兵圍之，令諸臣以次出外，出輒殺之，凡殺四十二人。

translations.literal: When they arrived troops surrounded them and ordered the ministers to go out one by one; as each went out he was killed—forty-two in all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Troops surrounded them; each who left was killed—forty-two in all.

sentences.zh: 國璽及在、天波、吉翔、國泰、華亭侯王維恭、綏寧伯蒲纓、都督馬雄飛、吏部侍郎鄧士廉等皆預焉。

translations.literal: Guoxi, Zai, Tianbo, Jixiang, Guotai, the marquis Wang Weigong, the earl Pu Ying, the regional commander Ma Xiongfei, the vice minister Deng Shilian, and others were among them.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxi, Zai, Tianbo, Jixiang, Guotai, Wang Weigong, Pu Ying, Ma Xiongfei, Deng Shilian, and others perished.

sentences.zh: 惟都督同知鄧凱以傷足不行，獲免。

translations.literal: Only the regional vice commander Deng Kai, injured in the foot, did not go and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Only Deng Kai, lame, stayed away and lived.

sentences.zh: 時順冶十八年七月也。

translations.literal: It was the seventh month of the eighteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was the seventh month of Shunzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 自是由榔左右無人。

translations.literal: From then on Youlang had no one at his side.
translations.idiomatic: From then the Prince had no one left.

sentences.zh: 至十二月，緬人遂送之出境，事具國史。

translations.literal: By the twelfth month the Burmese sent him beyond the border; the full account is in the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Burmese sent him out of the country; the national history records the rest.

sentences.zh: 初，由榔之走緬甸也，昆明諸生薛大觀嘆息曰：「不能背城戰，君臣同死社稷，顧欲走蠻邦以茍活，不重可羞耶！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Youlang fled to Burma, the student Xue Daguan of Kunming sighed and said: "Unable to fight with our backs to the wall and die with the altars of state together, yet wishing to flee to a barbarian land to live on in shame—is this not doubly shameful!
translations.idiomatic: When Youlang fled to Burma, Xue Daguan of Kunming said: "To flee to barbarians rather than die for the altars is doubly shameful.

sentences.zh: 」顧子之翰曰：「吾不惜七尺軀，為天下明大義，汝其勉之！

translations.literal: " He looked at his son Zhihan and said: "I do not begrudge my seven-foot frame to make the great principle clear to the world—you must strive!
translations.idiomatic: He told his son Zhihan: "I give my life to clarify duty for the world—strive on.

sentences.zh: 」之翰曰：「大人死忠，兒當死孝。

translations.literal: " Zhihan said: "When the father dies for loyalty, the son should die for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihan said: "Father dies loyal; son dies filial.

sentences.zh: 」大觀曰：「汝有母在。

translations.literal: " Daguan said: "You have a mother still living.
translations.idiomatic: Daguan said: "Your mother lives.

sentences.zh: 」時其母適在旁，顧之翰妻曰：「彼父子能死忠孝，吾兩人獨不能死節義耶？

translations.literal: " His mother was just at hand; Zhihan's wife said: "If father and son can die for loyalty and filial piety, can we two alone not die for chastity and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: His wife said: "If they die for loyalty and filial piety, shall we not die for righteousness?

sentences.zh: 」其侍女方抱幼子，問曰：「主人皆死，何以處我？

translations.literal: " Their serving maid, just holding an infant, asked: "The masters all die—what is to be done with me?
translations.idiomatic: The maid with an infant asked what would become of her.

sentences.zh: 」大觀曰：「爾能死，甚善。

translations.literal: " Daguan said: "If you can die, it is very good.
translations.idiomatic: Daguan said: "If you can die, well.

sentences.zh: 」於是五人偕赴城北黑龍潭死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the five together went to Black Dragon Pool north of the city and died.
translations.idiomatic: All five drowned themselves at Black Dragon Pool north of the city.

sentences.zh: 次日，諸屍相牽浮水上，幼子在侍女懷中，兩手堅抱如故。

translations.literal: The next day the corpses floated linked on the water; the infant in the maid's arms still clasped in both hands as before.
translations.idiomatic: Next day their bodies floated linked; the infant still clasped in the maid's arms.

sentences.zh: 大觀次女已適人，避兵山中，相去數十里，亦同日赴火死。

translations.literal: Daguan's second daughter had married and was avoiding soldiers in the mountains several tens of li away; on the same day she too went to the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: His married daughter in the hills died by fire the same day.

sentences.zh: 有那嵩者，沅江土官也。

translations.literal: There was Na Song, a tribal official of Yuanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Na Song was a Yuanjiang tribal official.

sentences.zh: 世為知府。

translations.literal: His family for generations were prefects.
translations.idiomatic: His house had held the prefecture for generations.

sentences.zh: 嵩嗣職，循法無過。

translations.literal: Song succeeded to office and followed the law without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Song succeeded without fault under the law.

sentences.zh: 王走緬甸，過沅江，嵩與子燾迎謁，供奉甚謹，設宴皆金銀器。

translations.literal: When the Prince fled to Burma and passed Yuanjiang, Song with his son Tao met and attended him very carefully, setting out banquets all in gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince passed Yuanjiang, Song and his son Tao received him with gold and silver banquets.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，悉以獻，曰：「此行上供者少，聊以佐缺乏耳。

translations.literal: When the feast ended they presented everything, saying: "On this journey what is offered above is little; this is merely to help what is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: They gave all away, saying: "For the journey this is but a small aid.

sentences.zh: 」後李定國號召諸土司兵，嵩即起兵應之。

translations.literal: " Later when Li Dingguo called up tribal troops, Song at once raised troops in answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingguo called the tribes, Song raised troops.

sentences.zh: 已而城破，登樓自焚，闔家皆死，其士民亦多巷戰死。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; he ascended a tower and burned himself, and his whole household died; many of his soldiers and people also died fighting in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell; he burned himself on a tower with his household; many died in the streets.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明自神宗而後，浸微浸滅，不可復振。

translations.literal: The commentator says: From the Shenzong emperor onward the Ming gradually declined and could not be revived.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: From Shenzong the Ming waned beyond revival.

sentences.zh: 揆厥所由，國是紛呶，朝端水火，寧坐視社稷之淪胥，而不能破除門戶之角立。

translations.literal: Tracing the cause, national policy was clamorous and court factions were fire and water; they would rather watch the altars of state sink than break down the corners of factional rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: National policy was chaos and court factions war; they watched the altars sink rather than end faction.

sentences.zh: 故至桂林播越，旦夕不支，而吳、楚之樹黨相傾，猶仍南都翻案之故態也。

translations.literal: Thus even when driven to wander at Guilin, facing collapse morning and night, the Wu and Chu factions still strove against each other, still the old habit of the southern capital's case reversals.
translations.idiomatic: Even at Guilin on the brink, Wu and Chu factions still fought as at the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 顛覆之端，有自來矣，於當時任事諸臣何責哉。

translations.literal: The beginnings of overturn were long in coming; what blame can be laid on the ministers who bore office at the time?
translations.idiomatic: The seeds of ruin were long sown; how can the ministers of that hour be blamed?
